files.name: TimedEventsManager.verse
files.code:
# ========================================================================================
# TimedEventsManager.verse
# Summary: T-051 Timed Events Manager. Generic scheduling engine for timed events (OneShot / Recurring / Hybrid
#   via one @editable enum+struct config; only OneShot is implemented, Recurring/Hybrid are safe scaffolds that log a
#   CRITICAL warning and never start an undefined countdown). Exposes EventStarted/EventEnded Verse events per event plus
#   optional native trigger_device fields (OnStartTrigger/OnEndTrigger) so any device can be bound from the Details panel.
#   One shared widget, WBP_TimedEventCountdown (placed/bound by the owner; never created via MCP), shows a 3-phase
#   lifecycle driven by the single device-level WatchWidgetPhases coroutine: StatusMsg "Next event start in: " + Timer to
#   StartUnix, then "Event in progress" + Timer to EndUnix, then the nearest future OneShot, else "No event right now" / 00:00:00:00.
#   Widget fields are written only when the text changed (T-107).
#   EventName/EventDescription are written once per event start by WatchStart (EventDescription needs its own MVVM View
#   Binding on the Widget Blueprint - owner action, not a Verse issue). First event: "Bring a Friend" (UTC one-shot).
# Last modified: 2026-11-05 - v11
# ========================================================================================

using { /Fortnite.com/Devices }
using { /Verse.org/Simulation }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/Diagnostics }
using { shared_utils }

# Centralized logger (kit rule 2)
@editable DebugLoggingEnabled_TimedEvents : logic = false
Log_TimedEvents(LogMessage : string):void=
    if (DebugLoggingEnabled_TimedEvents?):
        Print(LogMessage)

# T-052: string->message conversion helper for the shared widget's fields (same <localizes>
# pattern already used project-wide, e.g. LikeFavWorldUI.verse's S2M).
S2M_TimedEvents<localizes>(Value : string) : message = "{Value}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# BUG FIX (this pass, 2026-09-19): DateToUnixTime used to live in Event_Timer.verse, which was
# deleted on 2026-09-19 (see project memory event_timer_deleted_2026-09-19.md) without checking
# that this file still called it - left 8 call sites referencing an identifier that no longer
# existed anywhere in the project (compile error 3506, "Unknown identifier `DateToUnixTime`").
# Reimplemented locally so this file has no dependency on Event_Timer_Device again. UTC,
# proleptic Gregorian calendar, no int/int division (Verse `/` on int yields a rational, not an
# int - see WriteCountdownToWidget's own comment on the same gotcha further down this file) -
# days are accumulated with `for` loops instead.
# BUG FIX (B-024, 2026-09-19): this <decides> function's branches used to terminate in bare
# `true`/`false` literals. A `logic` literal by itself is NOT a decidable expression in Verse -
# only comparisons/queries (`A = B`, a `logic` converted with the `?` query operator) actually
# fail/succeed a <decides> function - so the literal `false` branch never made the function fail;
# it always succeeded regardless of which branch ran, making IsLeapYear_TimedEvents report EVERY
# year as a leap year (confirmed live via a temporary debug log: 2026-01-01 computed as 56*366
# days instead of the correct 56 years/14 real leap years = 20454 days - an exact 42-day
# overcount, matching the reported "42 days" bug). Fix: convert the `logic` literals to actual
# decides outcomes with the `?` query operator (`true?` succeeds, `false?` fails) instead of
# leaving them as inert values - keeps the original <decides> shape/call sites, only the two
# literal branches change.
IsLeapYear_TimedEvents(Year : int)<decides><transacts>:void=
    if(Mod[Year, 4] = 0):
        if(Mod[Year, 100] = 0):
            Mod[Year, 400] = 0
        else:
            true?
    else:
        false?

DaysInMonth_TimedEvents(Year : int, Month : int) : int=
    case(Month):
        1 => 31
        2 => if(IsLeapYear_TimedEvents[Year]) then 29 else 28
        3 => 31
        4 => 30
        5 => 31
        6 => 30
        7 => 31
        8 => 31
        9 => 30
        10 => 31
        11 => 30
        12 => 31
        _ => 30

DateToUnixTime(Year : int, Month : int, Day : int, Hour : int, Minute : int, Second : int) : int=
    var TotalDays : int = 0
    if(Year >= 1970):
        for(Y := 1970..Year - 1):
            set TotalDays = TotalDays + (if(IsLeapYear_TimedEvents[Y]) then 366 else 365)
    else:
        for(Y := Year..1969):
            set TotalDays = TotalDays - (if(IsLeapYear_TimedEvents[Y]) then 366 else 365)

    for(M := 1..Month - 1):
        set TotalDays = TotalDays + DaysInMonth_TimedEvents(Year, M)

    set TotalDays = TotalDays + (Day - 1)

    TotalDays * 86400 + Hour * 3600 + Minute * 60 + Second

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scheduling model: one enum + one config struct covers all 3 event shapes, so adding a new
# timed event never requires a new class - only a new array entry in timed_events_manager.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
timed_event_schedule_type := enum:
    OneShot
    Recurring
    Hybrid

timed_event_config := struct<concrete>:
    @editable
    EventName : string = "Unnamed Event"
    # T-052: shown on the shared WBP_TimedEventCountdown widget alongside EventName.
    @editable
    EventDescription : string = ""
    @editable
    ScheduleType : timed_event_schedule_type = timed_event_schedule_type.OneShot

    # OneShot window (UTC, absolute) - fully implemented this pass
    @editable
    StartYear : int = 2026
    @editable
    StartMonth : int = 1
    @editable
    StartDay : int = 1
    @editable
    StartHour : int = 0
    @editable
    StartMinute : int = 0
    @editable
    StartSecond : int = 0
    @editable
    EndYear : int = 2026
    @editable
    EndMonth : int = 1
    @editable
    EndDay : int = 2
    @editable
    EndHour : int = 0
    @editable
    EndMinute : int = 0
    @editable
    EndSecond : int = 0

    # Recurring window (UTC) - SCAFFOLD ONLY (T-051): fields exist and are editable, but the
    # calculation is not implemented/tested yet. Selecting this type logs a CRITICAL warning
    # and the countdown does not start, instead of running undefined/incorrect math.
    @editable
    RecurringPeriodSeconds : float = 604800.0
    @editable
    RecurringDurationSeconds : float = 86400.0

    # Hybrid daily/weekly band (UTC) - SCAFFOLD ONLY (T-051), same safety behavior as above.
    @editable
    HybridDailyStartHour : int = 13
    @editable
    HybridDailyEndHour : int = 17

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-event runtime: owns one config, exposes the on/off event pair, and (optionally) fires
# native trigger_device fields so presentation/Analytics can be bound purely in the editor.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
timed_events_engine := class:
    @editable
    Config : timed_event_config = timed_event_config{}
    @editable
    OnStartTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}
    @editable
    OnEndTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}

    # Public baseline on/off pair - the contract every future timed event reacts to.
    EventStarted<public> : event() = event(){}
    EventEnded<public> : event() = event(){}

    Run()<suspends>:void=
        case(Config.ScheduleType):
            timed_event_schedule_type.OneShot =>
                RunOneShot()
            timed_event_schedule_type.Recurring =>
                Log_TimedEvents("CRITICAL TimedEventsManager: event '{Config.EventName}' is configured as Recurring, which is a scaffold-only type (T-051). Countdown NOT started.")
            timed_event_schedule_type.Hybrid =>
                Log_TimedEvents("CRITICAL TimedEventsManager: event '{Config.EventName}' is configured as Hybrid, which is a scaffold-only type (T-051). Countdown NOT started.")

    RunOneShot()<suspends>:void=
        StartUnix := DateToUnixTime(Config.StartYear, Config.StartMonth, Config.StartDay, Config.StartHour, Config.StartMinute, Config.StartSecond)
        EndUnix := DateToUnixTime(Config.EndYear, Config.EndMonth, Config.EndDay, Config.EndHour, Config.EndMinute, Config.EndSecond)

        if(EndUnix <= StartUnix):
            Log_TimedEvents("CRITICAL TimedEventsManager: event '{Config.EventName}' has an invalid one-shot window (End <= Start). Refusing to start.")
            return

        if(NowAtBoot := Floor[GetSecondsSinceEpoch()]):
            if(NowAtBoot >= EndUnix):
                Log_TimedEvents("TimedEventsManager: event '{Config.EventName}' window already fully elapsed at server start; skipping this session.")
                return

            if(NowAtBoot < StartUnix):
                loop:
                    Sleep(1.0)
                    if(Floor[GetSecondsSinceEpoch()] >= StartUnix):
                        break

        Log_TimedEvents("TimedEventsManager: event '{Config.EventName}' STARTED.")
        # Native Trigger(Agent) firing is done by the owning device (it needs a
        # creative_object_interface context for GetPlayspace()) - see timed_events_manager's
        # WatchStart/WatchEnd, which subscribe to this event and fire the triggers per player.
        EventStarted.Signal()

        loop:
            Sleep(1.0)
            if(Floor[GetSecondsSinceEpoch()] >= EndUnix):
                break

        Log_TimedEvents("TimedEventsManager: event '{Config.EventName}' ENDED.")
        EventEnded.Signal()

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Device: @editable array of timed events. First entry is "Bring a Friend", precompiled with
# the owner-provided UTC values - purely cosmetic, no dependency on party_up_manager.verse.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
timed_events_manager := class(creative_device):
    # T-052: single shared widget instance (Scene Graph/entity API) - placed and bound by the
    # owner in the Details panel, this file never creates/places it via MCP. Optional: if left
    # unbound, WatchStart/WatchEnd/WatchWidgetPhases skip the widget write and log one warning
    # each, everything else (scheduling, native OnStartTrigger/OnEndTrigger) keeps working.
    @editable
    DisplayWidget : ?custom_verse.Event_Timer_System.WBP_TimedEventCountdown_entity = false

    @editable
    Events : []timed_events_engine = array{
        timed_events_engine{
            Config := timed_event_config{
                EventName := "Bring a Friend"
                EventDescription := "Invite a friend to play with you and unlock an exclusive bonus!"
                ScheduleType := timed_event_schedule_type.OneShot
                StartYear := 2026
                StartMonth := 9
                StartDay := 18
                StartHour := 14
                StartMinute := 0
                StartSecond := 0
                EndYear := 2026
                EndMonth := 9
                EndDay := 21
                EndHour := 14
                EndMinute := 0
                EndSecond := 0
            }
        }
    }

    # Last text written to the shared widget (see SetStatusIfChanged/SetTimerIfChanged).
    var LastStatusText : string = ""
    var LastTimerText : string = ""

    OnBegin<override>()<suspends>:void=
        # T-057: the widget's Timer/StatusMsg lifecycle is now driven by ONE device-level
        # coroutine with full visibility of the Events array (see WatchWidgetPhases below) -
        # spawned once, independent of any single event's EventStarted/EventEnded signals, so
        # there is no spawn-order dependency to get wrong here (unlike the per-engine loop
        # below, which still needs the T-056 ordering fix).
        spawn. WatchWidgetPhases()

        for(EventEngine : Events):
            # T-056 root-cause fix: WatchStart/WatchEnd MUST be spawned before Run(). `spawn.`
            # runs the new coroutine synchronously up to its own first suspension point before
            # returning control here, so spawning the awaiters first guarantees they are
            # blocked on EventStarted/EventEnded.Await() before Run() can reach Signal() - see
            # file header for the full analysis of the bug this fixes.
            spawn. WatchStart(EventEngine)
            spawn. WatchEnd(EventEngine)
            spawn. EventEngine.Run()

    # Fires the native OnStartTrigger once per player currently in the playspace, and writes
    # the shared widget's EventName/EventDescription (this file's Verse-side of both fields is
    # correct - see the T-057 header note on EventDescription's missing Widget Blueprint
    # binding). Lives on the device (creative_object_interface context) because GetPlayspace()
    # requires it - timed_events_engine itself is a plain class and can't call it directly.
    WatchStart(EventEngine : timed_events_engine)<suspends>:void=
        var HasWarnedMissingWidget : logic = false
        loop:
            EventEngine.EventStarted.Await()

            # T-052: single write of EventName/EventDescription to the shared widget, BEFORE
            # the native-trigger fan-out below (never inside the for - that would write once
            # per player). Last-write-wins across concurrent events is an accepted design
            # limitation, see file header. T-057: StatusMsg/Timer are intentionally NOT
            # touched here any more - WatchWidgetPhases owns those exclusively.
            if(Widget := DisplayWidget?):
                set Widget.EventName = S2M_TimedEvents(EventEngine.Config.EventName)
                set Widget.EventDescription = S2M_TimedEvents(EventEngine.Config.EventDescription)
                Log_TimedEvents("TimedEventsManager: widget updated for event '{EventEngine.Config.EventName}' START.")
            else if(not HasWarnedMissingWidget?):
                set HasWarnedMissingWidget = true
                Log_TimedEvents("WARNING TimedEventsManager: DisplayWidget is not bound - event '{EventEngine.Config.EventName}' START will not be shown on the shared widget.")

            for(Player : GetPlayspace().GetPlayers()):
                EventEngine.OnStartTrigger.Trigger(Player)

    # Fires the native OnEndTrigger once per player currently in the playspace. T-057: no
    # longer touches the shared widget at all - StatusMsg/Timer (including the "Event ended"
    # text and the fixed "00 : 00 : 00 : 00") are now owned end-to-end by WatchWidgetPhases,
    # which reacts to the same Events array rather than to this per-engine signal. This also
    # removes T-052's old "5s closure message then clear EventName/EventDescription" behavior
    # per T-057's acceptance criteria (replaced by the fixed Phase-3 state / Phase-1 handoff
    # to the next event).
    WatchEnd(EventEngine : timed_events_engine)<suspends>:void=
        loop:
            EventEngine.EventEnded.Await()
            Log_TimedEvents("TimedEventsManager: event '{EventEngine.Config.EventName}' ENDED - firing native OnEndTrigger fan-out.")
            for(Player : GetPlayspace().GetPlayers()):
                EventEngine.OnEndTrigger.Trigger(Player)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # T-057: 3-phase widget lifecycle controller. Unlike WatchStart/WatchEnd above (one
    # instance spawned per event, reacting to that single event's Verse events), this is
    # spawned exactly ONCE on the device and owns the widget's Timer+StatusMsg fields for
    # the entire Events array's lifetime - it needs that whole-array visibility to decide
    # "is there a next event" after one ends (see file header's architecture note).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    WatchWidgetPhases()<suspends>:void=
        var HasWarnedMissingWidget : logic = false
        loop:
            if(Widget := DisplayWidget?):
                if(NowUnix := Floor[GetSecondsSinceEpoch()]):
                    ActiveOpt := FindActiveEvent(NowUnix)
                    NextOpt := FindNextUpcomingEvent(NowUnix)
                    if(ActiveEngine := ActiveOpt?):
                        # Phase 2: an event's OneShot window currently contains NowUnix -
                        # covers both the normal case (Phase 1 counted down to it) and boot
                        # with an event already mid-window (owner clarification 3: skip
                        # straight here, never a negative/past-start countdown).
                        SetStatusIfChanged(Widget, "Event in progress")
                        EndUnix := DateToUnixTime(ActiveEngine.Config.EndYear, ActiveEngine.Config.EndMonth, ActiveEngine.Config.EndDay, ActiveEngine.Config.EndHour, ActiveEngine.Config.EndMinute, ActiveEngine.Config.EndSecond)
                        WriteCountdownToWidget(Widget, EndUnix, NowUnix)
                    else if(NextEngine := NextOpt?):
                        # Phase 1: no event active right now, but a future OneShot event
                        # exists - count down to ITS start (owner clarification 4: this is
                        # re-evaluated every tick from the whole array, so a just-ended event
                        # falls straight back into Phase 1 for the next one instead of
                        # sticking on Phase 3).
                        SetStatusIfChanged(Widget, "Next event start in: ")
                        StartUnix := DateToUnixTime(NextEngine.Config.StartYear, NextEngine.Config.StartMonth, NextEngine.Config.StartDay, NextEngine.Config.StartHour, NextEngine.Config.StartMinute, NextEngine.Config.StartSecond)
                        WriteCountdownToWidget(Widget, StartUnix, NowUnix)
                    else:
                        # Phase 3: no active event AND no future one configured - fixed,
                        # stable end state (owner clarification 4: only reached when nothing
                        # else in Events qualifies; with today's single "Bring a Friend"
                        # event this is where it lands after 2026-09-21 14:00 UTC).
                        # T-107: neutral wording, because with no event scheduled the board is
                        # shown for ever and "Event ended" read as a stale leftover.
                        SetStatusIfChanged(Widget, "No event right now")
                        SetTimerIfChanged(Widget, "00 : 00 : 00 : 00")
            else if(not HasWarnedMissingWidget?):
                set HasWarnedMissingWidget = true
                Log_TimedEvents("WARNING TimedEventsManager: DisplayWidget is not bound - the 3-phase Timer/StatusMsg lifecycle will not be shown on the shared widget.")
            Sleep(1.0)

    # Only OneShot events have a fully-implemented window (Recurring/Hybrid are scaffold-only,
    # see Run() above) - both scans below skip anything else, exactly mirroring what actually
    # gets a running countdown.
    FindActiveEvent(NowUnix : int):?timed_events_engine=
        var Found : ?timed_events_engine = false
        var HasFound : logic = false
        for(Engine : Events):
            if(not HasFound?, Engine.Config.ScheduleType = timed_event_schedule_type.OneShot):
                StartUnix := DateToUnixTime(Engine.Config.StartYear, Engine.Config.StartMonth, Engine.Config.StartDay, Engine.Config.StartHour, Engine.Config.StartMinute, Engine.Config.StartSecond)
                EndUnix := DateToUnixTime(Engine.Config.EndYear, Engine.Config.EndMonth, Engine.Config.EndDay, Engine.Config.EndHour, Engine.Config.EndMinute, Engine.Config.EndSecond)
                if(EndUnix > StartUnix, StartUnix <= NowUnix, NowUnix < EndUnix):
                    set Found = option{Engine}
                    set HasFound = true
        Found

    # Scans the whole array for the nearest FUTURE OneShot start, so the display can hand off
    # straight from Phase 3 into Phase 1 for it (owner clarification 4) instead of needing a
    # separate "what's next" pass elsewhere.
    FindNextUpcomingEvent(NowUnix : int):?timed_events_engine=
        var Best : ?timed_events_engine = false
        var BestStart : int = 0
        for(Engine : Events):
            if(Engine.Config.ScheduleType = timed_event_schedule_type.OneShot):
                StartUnix := DateToUnixTime(Engine.Config.StartYear, Engine.Config.StartMonth, Engine.Config.StartDay, Engine.Config.StartHour, Engine.Config.StartMinute, Engine.Config.StartSecond)
                EndUnix := DateToUnixTime(Engine.Config.EndYear, Engine.Config.EndMonth, Engine.Config.EndDay, Engine.Config.EndHour, Engine.Config.EndMinute, Engine.Config.EndSecond)
                if(EndUnix > StartUnix, StartUnix > NowUnix):
                    if(Best?):
                        if(StartUnix < BestStart):
                            set Best = option{Engine}
                            set BestStart = StartUnix
                    else:
                        set Best = option{Engine}
                        set BestStart = StartUnix
        Best

    # T-107: widget writes only when the text changed (the loop ticks every 1 s, but the
    # Phase 2/3 text and the 00:00:00:00 timer rarely change).
    SetStatusIfChanged(Widget : custom_verse.Event_Timer_System.WBP_TimedEventCountdown_entity, Text : string):void=
        if(Text <> LastStatusText):
            set LastStatusText = Text
            set Widget.StatusMsg = S2M_TimedEvents(Text)

    SetTimerIfChanged(Widget : custom_verse.Event_Timer_System.WBP_TimedEventCountdown_entity, Text : string):void=
        if(Text <> LastTimerText):
            set LastTimerText = Text
            set Widget.Timer = S2M_TimedEvents(Text)

    # Shared "DD : HH : MM : SS" countdown formatter, used for both Phase 1 (to StartUnix) and
    # Phase 2 (to EndUnix) - same Mod[Floor[...], N]/float-divisor pattern as T-056 (int
    # division in Verse yields a rational and always needs Floor[]+a float divisor).
    WriteCountdownToWidget(Widget : custom_verse.Event_Timer_System.WBP_TimedEventCountdown_entity, TargetUnix : int, NowUnix : int):void=
        RawRemaining := TargetUnix - NowUnix
        RemainingSeconds := if(RawRemaining > 0) then RawRemaining else 0
        RemainingSecondsF : float = RemainingSeconds * 1.0
        if(Days := Floor[RemainingSecondsF / 86400.0]):
            if(Hours := Mod[Floor[RemainingSecondsF / 3600.0], 24]):
                if(Minutes := Mod[Floor[RemainingSecondsF / 60.0], 60]):
                    if(Seconds := Mod[RemainingSeconds, 60]):
                        SetTimerIfChanged(Widget, "{ZeroPad2(Days)} : {ZeroPad2(Hours)} : {ZeroPad2(Minutes)} : {ZeroPad2(Seconds)}")

recipes.use: Built from the Verse code of GameManager.
steps: Copy the folder into the project, keep its folder structure
Place game_manager in the level
Assign the devices it needs and set the options in the Details panel
Launch a session and check it
devices: game_manager: the device to place in the level
RoundTimer: a timer_device
IntermissionTimer: a timer_device
ZombieSpawnerPools: a creature_spawner_device (pools are active per round, and kills are reported per pool via EliminatedEvent.)
RandomZombieSpawnerPools: a creature_spawner_device (report) - any number can be added/removed later without further code changes.)
RandomNpcSpawnerPools: a npc_spawner_device
RandomGuardSpawnerPools: a guard_spawner_device
InvasionSpawnerPools: a wildlife_spawner_device
KillTrigger: a trigger_device (a pure native device-to-device event binding, not a Verse call.)
BossRewardTrigger: a trigger_device (BossRewardTrigger instead of KillTrigger, so native kill Accolades don't fire either.)
RoundCompleteTrigger: a trigger_device (notification).)
RoundStartTrigger: a trigger_device (established for KillTrigger/RoundCompleteTrigger/DiamondEarnedTrigger.)
DiamondEarnedTrigger: a trigger_device (array) without GameManager knowing about or calling into that listener.)
RoundMessageDevice: a hud_message_device (player in one native call, not a per-agent loop) - see RunGameLoop/OnRoundCompleted below.)
GoldItemGranter: a item_granter_device (purely additive - the Verse balances were removed in T-107; the physical items are the only balance.)
DiamondItemGranter: a item_granter_device
GoldCounterButton: a conditional_button_device (ResourceCounterLoop below.)
DiamondCounterButton: a conditional_button_device
PlayerSpawners: a player_spawner_device (leave, so it cannot drive the reset-at-0-players rule on its own).)
settings: DebugLoggingEnabled (logic) = true: it compiles fine (v18 fix, see project memory).
DiagLoggingEnabled (logic) = false: (per-kill / per-signal lines); the call sites guard on it BEFORE the string is interpolated.
BaseGoldPerKill (int) = 5: formula against the equivalent zombie pool's PoolIndex - no separate NPC tuning.
EnableZombieMainPool (logic) = true: off. Default true so the current live island's behavior is unchanged.
EnableHive (logic) = true: for another device type, confirmed by owner). Default true, unchanged live behavior.
EnableBossSystem (logic) = true: triggered regardless of the gap/pool tuning above. Default true, unchanged live behavior.
BossKillBaseGold (int) = 100: the Boss @editable group for consistency (same placement rule as BossScalingFactor itself).
MaxBossRoundDuration (float) = 300.0: code is needed for that - RoundEndedEarly is only ever set true by WaitForAllPlayersDown()).
BossSpawnWarningTimeout (float) = 30.0: T-066: forwarded to boss_event_manager - see that file's own field comment for what it does.

# economy_ledger.verse
# Summary: Owns the gold/diamond reward calculation and physical item-granting calls for both currencies, extracted from game_manager.verse (T-042). It keeps no per-player
#   balances (removed in v9, T-107). A plain Verse class (NOT a creative_device) instantiated and configured by
#   game_manager via archetype (GoldItemGranter/DiamondItemGranter/BaseGoldPerKill/GoldPerKillStep/XPPerKill/DiamondsPerRoundCompleted stay @editable on game_manager,
#   since they are bound to the placed device in the Details panel).
# Last modified: 2026-11-05 — v9 (T-107A: removed unused PlayerGold/Diamonds/XP maps, InitPlayer, RemovePlayer)
#
#
# Notes (still valid):
#  - Scope decision (T-042): game_manager keeps KillTrigger/RoundCompleteTrigger/DiamondEarnedTrigger and the public GoldAwardedEvent/DiamondsAwardedEvent; it calls
#    this class only to update balances and grant physical items, then fires its own triggers/events with the amount returned. This keeps every external contract
#    (LeaderboardManager's GoldAwardedEvent.Await()/DiamondsAwardedEvent.Await(), other files' bindings to the SAME physical Trigger actors) unchanged. This class never
#    fires triggers/events itself.
#  - AwardRoundDiamonds is <decides> (returns the round diamond amount, no state); the physical grant is the separate GrantRoundDiamondItem, called by game_manager only when
#    AwardRoundDiamonds[Player] succeeds. EconomyLog/Print carries the no_rollback effect and cannot be called inside a <decides> function, so the log line
#    lives in GrantRoundDiamondItem.
#  - AwardBossKillRewards grants BOTH gold and diamonds in one call to every connected player when a boss event is won. The Players list comes from game_manager (a
#    plain Verse class cannot call GetPlayspace()). BossKillBaseGold/BossKillBaseDiamonds are scaled by the same Multiplier formula as boss_event_manager.SpawnBossFromEntry
#    (BossScalingFactor passed in from game_manager's own @editable; no second copy). The FULL reward goes to every player (not split), through the same
#    item granters; it returns (GoldReward, DiamondReward) so game_manager fires its triggers/events per player.
using { /Fortnite.com/Devices }
using { /Fortnite.com/Game }
using { /Fortnite.com/Characters }
using { /Verse.org/Simulation }
using { big_number_utils }
using { shared_utils }
using { player_state_utils }

economy_ledger := class:

    # Own centralized logger (same pattern as horde_scaler.verse/coin_display_manager.verse) -
    # independent from game_manager's own Log, deliberately not referencing game_manager back to
    # avoid a circular class dependency for something as small as a log line.
    var EconomyDebugLoggingEnabled : logic = false
    EconomyLog(LogMessage : string) : void=
        if (EconomyDebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Print(LogMessage)

    # --- Device references and tuning, set via archetype by game_manager at construction ---
    GoldItemGranter : item_granter_device
    DiamondItemGranter : item_granter_device
    BaseGoldPerKill : int
    GoldPerKillStep : int
    XPPerKill : int
    DiamondsPerRoundCompleted : int

    # --- T-030 FOLLOW-UP #2: boss-kill reward tuning, mirrored from game_manager's own
    # @editable Boss group (BossKillBaseGold/BossKillBaseDiamonds are new fields there;
    # BossScalingFactor is the SAME field already passed to boss_event_manager, not a
    # duplicate) - see AwardBossKillRewards below. ---
    BossKillBaseGold : int
    BossKillBaseDiamonds : int
    BossScalingFactor : float

    # T-107: the PlayerGold/PlayerDiamonds/PlayerXP maps were removed - nothing ever read them
    # (the real balances are the physical Gold/Diamond items; the HUD counts those).

    # --- Gold + XP reward on zombie kill ---
    # Returns the exact gold Reward computed/awarded, so the caller (game_manager.AwardAndSignalKill, shared by zombie and NPC kills,
    # OnZombieEliminated/OnNpcEliminated via AwardAndSignalKill) can Signal its own GoldAwardedEvent with the right amount and fire
    # KillTrigger - same formula/order of operations as GameManager.verse v27, only relocated.
    AwardKillRewards(Killer : agent, PoolIndex : int, CurrentRound : int) : int=
        BaseReward : int = BaseGoldPerKill + GoldPerKillStep * PoolIndex
        Reward := BaseReward + 2 * CurrentRound
        EconomyLog("economy_ledger: awarded {Reward} gold to a player for a zombie kill (round {CurrentRound})")

        # v11: physical grant of the same Reward amount as a real Gold item, in parallel with
        # the Verse balance above (additive only - see GameManager.verse's own v11 header note).
        set GoldItemGranter.DefaultItemCount = Reward
        GoldItemGranter.GrantItem(Killer)
        EconomyLog("economy_ledger: physically granted {Reward} Gold item(s) to the killer via GoldItemGranter")

        # XP: flat XPPerKill, same per-player map pattern as gold.
        EconomyLog("economy_ledger: awarded {XPPerKill} XP for a zombie kill")

        Reward

    # --- Diamonds on round completion (per player) ---
    # Called once per currently active player by game_manager.OnRoundCompleted's own loop.
    # v2 (T-042 resubmission, 2026-09-12): split back into the same two-step shape v27 actually
    # needed. Verse forbids calling a <no_rollback> effect (GrantItem) from inside a function
    # that is still <decides> (a decides failure after a no_rollback call would have to roll
    # back an effect that, by definition, can't be undone) - that combination is what didn't
    # compile when both were merged into one <decides> function. The fix keeps the gating
    # instead of dropping it: AwardRoundDiamonds stays <decides> and does ONLY the balance
    # update (map write only, no no_rollback effect inside it); the physical grant moved to its
    # own always-succeeds GrantRoundDiamondItem, which the caller (game_manager.OnRoundCompleted)
    # now only invokes - together with DiamondEarnedTrigger/DiamondsAwardedEvent - when the
    # decides call above actually succeeds (bracket-call `if (Amount := ...AwardRoundDiamonds[Player]):`).
    # This restores v27's original gating mechanism byte-for-byte in shape, even though in
    # practice a map `set` on a var map never fails - the point is the trigger/event no longer
    # fire unconditionally regardless of the balance-update outcome.
    # Note: EconomyLog itself wraps Print, which also carries the 'no_rollback' effect - so it
    # can't be called from inside this <decides> function either (same constraint as GrantItem
    # below), not just for the map write. Logging for this path was moved to
    # GrantRoundDiamondItem, which only runs after this decides call has already succeeded.
    AwardRoundDiamonds(Player : player)<decides><transacts> : int=
        DiamondsPerRoundCompleted

    # v2: physical Diamond item grant, split out of AwardRoundDiamonds above so its
    # 'no_rollback' effect (GrantItem, and EconomyLog/Print - see note above) never lives
    # inside a <decides> function. Called by game_manager only after AwardRoundDiamonds[Player]
    # has already succeeded - see its comment above.
    GrantRoundDiamondItem(Player : player) : void=
        EconomyLog("economy_ledger: round diamonds awarded to a player")
        set DiamondItemGranter.DefaultItemCount = DiamondsPerRoundCompleted
        DiamondItemGranter.GrantItem(Player)
        EconomyLog("economy_ledger: physically granted {DiamondsPerRoundCompleted} Diamond item(s) to a player for completing a round")

    # --- Boss-kill reward (T-030 FOLLOW-UP #2) ---
    # Called once by game_manager right after a boss round that did NOT end via an all-players-down wipe
    # (boss(es) defeated, or the MaxBossRoundDuration soft-win timeout; gated by `not RoundEndedEarly?`). Grants the FULL BossKillBaseGold/
    # BossKillBaseDiamonds reward, scaled by the same Multiplier formula boss_event_manager.
    # SpawnBossFromEntry uses for HP/shield (1.0 + RoundNumber * BossScalingFactor), to every
    # player in the supplied Players list (not split/divided among them). Takes Players directly
    # rather than reaching for GetPlayspace() itself - this class is a plain Verse class, same
    # "cannot call GetPlayspace()" constraint documented in boss_event_manager.verse's header, so
    # game_manager (a real device) supplies the list, same shape AwardKillRewards/
    # AwardRoundDiamonds already use for a single Player/Killer.
    # RoundFloatToInt now comes from the shared shared_utils module (T-080) - boss reward amounts
    # are always non-negative (BossKillBaseGold/BossKillBaseDiamonds >= 0, Multiplier >= 1.0), so
    # its +0.5 half-up bias is correct.

    AwardBossKillRewards<public>(Players : []player, RoundNumber : int) : tuple(int, int)=
        Multiplier := 1.0 + IntToFloat(RoundNumber) * BossScalingFactor
        GoldReward : int = RoundFloatToInt(IntToFloat(BossKillBaseGold) * Multiplier)
        DiamondReward : int = RoundFloatToInt(IntToFloat(BossKillBaseDiamonds) * Multiplier)
        for (Player : Players):
            if (PlayerAgent := agent[Player]):
                set GoldItemGranter.DefaultItemCount = GoldReward
                GoldItemGranter.GrantItem(PlayerAgent)
                set DiamondItemGranter.DefaultItemCount = DiamondReward
                DiamondItemGranter.GrantItem(PlayerAgent)
        EconomyLog("economy_ledger: boss defeated (round {RoundNumber}, multiplier {Multiplier}) - awarded {GoldReward} gold + {DiamondReward} diamonds to {Players.Length} connected player(s)")
        (GoldReward, DiamondReward)

# horde_scaler.verse
# Summary: Owns the zombie/NPC horde scaling logic extracted from game_manager.verse (T-042): EnableHordeForRound/DisableAllHorde, the deterministic per-pool
#   activation-round formula and the independent per-pool random-activation rolls. A plain Verse class (NOT a creative_device) instantiated and configured by game_manager
#   via archetype; the pool arrays and tuning fields (ZombieSpawnerPools/RandomZombieSpawnerPools/RandomPoolMinRound/RandomPoolActivationChance, NPC pools, Enable* toggles)
#   stay @editable on game_manager (bound to the placed device) and are received here at construction.
# Last modified: 2026-11-05 — v6 (T-103: debug logging off by default)
#
#
# Notes (still valid):
#  - game_manager calls HordeScaler.EnableHordeForRound(CurrentRound) / DisableAllHorde() at the same points in RunGameLoop. This class owns only spawn/despawn scheduling,
#    never reward math (NPC kill-reward parity lives in GameManager.verse).
#  - Four arrays (Zombie main/random, NPC main/random) are each gated by their own EnableZombieMainPool/EnableNpcMainPool/EnableZombieRandomPool/EnableNpcRandomPool flag,
#    received by archetype from game_manager (not @editable here). NPC pools use the SAME per-index (1 + 2*Index) activation formula and per-round roll
#    (RandomPoolActivationChance) as the zombie pools; no extra tuning fields.
#  - NPC pools are []npc_spawner_device (guard_spawner_device was the wrong type). npc_spawner_device has no no-arg Despawn(), only DespawnAll(Instigator:?agent), so
#    DisableAllHorde cleans NPC pools with DespawnAll(false) + Disable() (Enable()/Disable() exist on both device types); zombie pools use EliminateCreatures() + Disable().
using { /Fortnite.com/Devices }
using { /Verse.org/Random }

horde_scaler := class:

    # Own centralized logger (same pattern as coin_display_manager.verse's
    # CoinDisplayDebugLoggingEnabled/CoinDisplayLog) - independent from game_manager's own Log,
    # deliberately not referencing game_manager back to avoid a circular class dependency for
    # something as small as a log line.
    var HordeDebugLoggingEnabled : logic = false
    HordeLog(LogMessage : string) : void=
        if (HordeDebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Print(LogMessage)

    # --- Device references, set via archetype by game_manager at construction (arrays first,
    # zombie/NPC pairs grouped together) ---
    ZombieSpawnerPools : []creature_spawner_device
    NpcSpawnerPools : []npc_spawner_device
    RandomZombieSpawnerPools : []creature_spawner_device
    RandomNpcSpawnerPools : []npc_spawner_device
    GuardSpawnerPools : []guard_spawner_device
    RandomGuardSpawnerPools : []guard_spawner_device

    # --- Tuning, set via archetype by game_manager at construction (shared by both the zombie
    # and NPC random pools - no separate NPC tuning fields needed) ---
    RandomPoolMinRound : int
    RandomPoolActivationChance : float

    # --- Per-array enable toggles (T-058), set via archetype by game_manager at construction -
    # each independently gates its own array; any combination (both on, either alone, both off)
    # is valid, no mutual exclusivity between the zombie and NPC variant of a given pool. ---
    EnableZombieMainPool : logic
    EnableNpcMainPool : logic
    EnableZombieRandomPool : logic
    EnableNpcRandomPool : logic
    EnableGuardMainPool : logic
    EnableGuardRandomPool : logic

    # --- Horde scaling (verbatim from GameManager.verse v27, T-058 added the NPC pools/toggles
    # alongside the pre-existing zombie logic with no change to the zombie branches themselves)
    # Pool `Index` activates starting at round `1 + 2*Index` (pool 0 -> round 1, pool 1 ->
    # round 3, pool 2 -> round 5, ...), avoiding integer division entirely. The NPC main pool
    # uses the exact same formula against its own Index, independent of the zombie array's
    # length.
    EnableHordeForRound(RoundNumber : int) : void=
        if (EnableZombieMainPool?):
            for (Index -> Spawner : ZombieSpawnerPools):
                ActivationRound := 1 + 2 * Index
                if (RoundNumber >= ActivationRound):
                    Spawner.Enable()
                    HordeLog("horde_scaler: enabled zombie pool {Index} for round {RoundNumber}")
        if (EnableNpcMainPool?):
            for (Index -> Spawner : NpcSpawnerPools):
                ActivationRound := 1 + 2 * Index
                if (RoundNumber >= ActivationRound):
                    Spawner.Enable()
                    HordeLog("horde_scaler: enabled npc pool {Index} for round {RoundNumber}")
        # T-098: guard_spawner_device main pool, same per-index formula (own Index, independent of other arrays).
        if (EnableGuardMainPool?):
            for (Index -> Spawner : GuardSpawnerPools):
                ActivationRound := 1 + 2 * Index
                if (RoundNumber >= ActivationRound):
                    Spawner.Enable()
                    HordeLog("horde_scaler: enabled guard pool {Index} for round {RoundNumber}")
        # Random pools: from RandomPoolMinRound onward, EACH pool in the array rolls its own
        # independent RandomPoolActivationChance this round - one spawner's roll has no bearing
        # on any other's, so any subset (or all, or none) of the placed random pools may be
        # active in a given round. Zombie and NPC random pools roll completely independently of
        # each other (separate loops, separate rolls) - only their shared RandomPoolMinRound
        # gate and RandomPoolActivationChance value come from the same tuning fields.
        if (RoundNumber >= RandomPoolMinRound):
            if (EnableZombieRandomPool?):
                for (Index -> Spawner : RandomZombieSpawnerPools):
                    Roll := GetRandomFloat(0.0, 1.0)
                    if (Roll <= RandomPoolActivationChance):
                        Spawner.Enable()
                        HordeLog("horde_scaler: random zombie pool {Index} activated for round {RoundNumber} (roll {Roll} <= chance {RandomPoolActivationChance})")
            if (EnableNpcRandomPool?):
                for (Index -> Spawner : RandomNpcSpawnerPools):
                    Roll := GetRandomFloat(0.0, 1.0)
                    if (Roll <= RandomPoolActivationChance):
                        Spawner.Enable()
                        HordeLog("horde_scaler: random npc pool {Index} activated for round {RoundNumber} (roll {Roll} <= chance {RandomPoolActivationChance})")
            if (EnableGuardRandomPool?):
                for (Index -> Spawner : RandomGuardSpawnerPools):
                    Roll := GetRandomFloat(0.0, 1.0)
                    if (Roll <= RandomPoolActivationChance):
                        Spawner.Enable()
                        HordeLog("horde_scaler: random guard pool {Index} activated for round {RoundNumber} (roll {Roll} <= chance {RandomPoolActivationChance})")

    # Cleanup always runs unconditionally against every array regardless of the Enable* toggles
    # (EliminateCreatures()/DespawnAll(false) plus Disable() on a spawner that was never enabled this round is a harmless no-op) -
    # simpler and safer than mirroring the toggle checks here, and matches the pre-T-058 shape
    # where DisableAllHorde never checked any condition either.
    DisableAllHorde() : void=
        for (Spawner : ZombieSpawnerPools):
            Spawner.EliminateCreatures()
            Spawner.Disable()
        for (Spawner : NpcSpawnerPools):
            Spawner.DespawnAll(false)
            Spawner.Disable()
        for (Spawner : RandomZombieSpawnerPools):
            Spawner.EliminateCreatures()
            Spawner.Disable()
        for (Spawner : RandomNpcSpawnerPools):
            Spawner.DespawnAll(false)
            Spawner.Disable()
        for (Spawner : GuardSpawnerPools):
            Spawner.Despawn()
            Spawner.Disable()
        for (Spawner : RandomGuardSpawnerPools):
            Spawner.Despawn()
            Spawner.Disable()
        HordeLog("horde_scaler: despawned/disabled all zombie and npc pools (including random pools) at round end")

# MapCode.verse
# Summary: Reusable HUD bar showing the island name/code (alternating with a Favorite/Like prompt) for every player, with 10 selectable styles, size/offset and floating animation.
# Last modified: 2026-11-05 - v5

using { /Fortnite.com/Devices }
using { /Verse.org/Simulation }
using { /Verse.org/Colors }
using { /Verse.org/Assets }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/UI }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/SpatialMath }

island_map_code_style<public> := enum:
    Rainbow
    Legendary
    OnyxGold
    Epic
    Pearl
    Rare
    Crimson
    Emerald
    Candy
    Teal

island_map_code_look := class:
    Wing : material
    Hex : material
    Badge : material
    NameColor : color_alpha
    CodeColor : color_alpha
    IconColor : color_alpha
    GlyphColor : color_alpha
    GlintColor : color_alpha
    RainbowName : logic = false

Tint(Hex : string) : color_alpha =
    C := MakeColorFromHex(Hex)
    color_alpha:
        Color := color:
            R := 2.521686 * C.R - 1.134131 * C.G - 0.387555 * C.B
            G := -0.276480 * C.R + 1.372719 * C.G - 0.096239 * C.B
            B := -0.015378 * C.R - 0.152975 * C.G + 1.168353 * C.B
        A := 1.0

ToMessage<localizes>(Text : string) : message = "{Text}"

MapNameTip<localizes> : message = "Name of the map."
MapCodeTip<localizes> : message = "Island code, for example 1234-5678-9012."
StyleTip<localizes> : message = "Look of the bar."
SwitchEveryTip<localizes> : message = "Seconds before it switches between the name and code and Favorite and Like (minimum 2 seconds)."
OffsetXTip<localizes> : message = "Moves the bar right, in pixels (1080p). Use a negative number to move it left."
OffsetYTip<localizes> : message = "Moves the bar down, in pixels (1080p). Use a negative number to move it up."
SizeTip<localizes> : message = "Size of the bar. 1.0 is the original size."
SizeXTip<localizes> : message = "Width of the bar. 1.0 is the original width."
SizeYTip<localizes> : message = "Height of the bar. 1.0 is the original height."
FloatHeightTip<localizes> : message = "How far the bar floats up and down, in pixels (0 to 10). 0 turns it off."
FloatSpeedTip<localizes> : message = "How fast it floats. 1.0 is normal, 2.0 is twice as fast."

island_map_code<public> := class(creative_device):

    @editable{ToolTip is MapNameTip}
    MapName : string = "MAP NAME"

    @editable{ToolTip is MapCodeTip}
    MapCode : string = "0000-0000-0000"

    @editable{ToolTip is StyleTip}
    Style : island_map_code_style = island_map_code_style.Rainbow

    @editable{ToolTip is SwitchEveryTip}
    SwitchEvery : float = 10.0

    @editable{ToolTip is OffsetXTip}
    OffsetX : float = 0.0

    @editable{ToolTip is OffsetYTip}
    OffsetY : float = 0.0

    @editable{ToolTip is SizeTip}
    Size : float = 1.0

    @editable{ToolTip is SizeXTip}
    SizeX : float = 1.0

    @editable{ToolTip is SizeYTip}
    SizeY : float = 1.0

    @editable{ToolTip is FloatHeightTip}
    FloatHeight : int = 4

    @editable{ToolTip is FloatSpeedTip}
    FloatSpeed : float = 1.0

    @editable DebugLoggingEnabled : logic = true

    Log(LogMessage : string) : void =
        if (DebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Print(LogMessage)

    # Device startup: attach the bar to current and future players
    OnBegin<override>()<suspends> : void =
        Playspace := GetPlayspace()
        for (Player : Playspace.GetPlayers()):
            spawn { RunFor(Player) }
        loop:
            Player := Playspace.PlayerAddedEvent().Await()
            spawn { RunFor(Player) }

    RunFor(Player : player)<suspends> : void =
        race:
            WaitForLeave(Player)
            block:
                # v3 (T-076): keep retrying (each attempt waits up to 10s for the player UI) instead
                # of giving up after the first 10s; the race with WaitForLeave ends it on leave.
                loop:
                    WaitForScreen(Player)
                    Added := AddBar(Player)
                    if (Bar := Added?):
                        Cycle(Bar)
                        break
                    Log("island_map_code: player UI not ready yet, retrying")

    WaitForLeave(Player : player)<suspends> : void =
        loop:
            Left := GetPlayspace().PlayerRemovedEvent().Await()
            if (Left = Player):
                break

    WaitForScreen(Player : player)<suspends> : void =
        var Waited : float = 0.0
        loop:
            if (Player.IsActive[], GetPlayerUI[Player]):
                break
            if (Waited >= 10.0):
                break
            Sleep(0.05)
            set Waited += 0.05

    AddBar(Player : player) : ?Widgets.WBP_HexMapCode =
        if (Player.IsActive[], Screen := GetPlayerUI[Player]):
            Bar := MakeBar()
            Screen.AddWidget(Place(Bar), player_ui_slot{ ZOrder := 30, InputMode := ui_input_mode.None })
            return option{Bar}
        Log("island_map_code: player UI not available, bar not added")
        false

    Cycle(Bar : Widgets.WBP_HexMapCode)<suspends> : void =
        Wait := Max(SwitchEvery, 2.0)
        loop:
            Sleep(Wait)
            set Bar.ShowName = 1.0
            set Bar.ShowLike = 0.0
            Sleep(Wait)
            set Bar.ShowLike = 1.0
            set Bar.ShowName = 0.0

    MakeBar() : Widgets.WBP_HexMapCode =
        Look := LookOf(Style)
        Name := ToMessage(MapName)
        Code := ToMessage(MapCode)
        Wide := Clamp(SizeX, 0.1, 9.9)
        Tall := Clamp(SizeY, 0.1, 9.9)
        Rise := Clamp(FloatHeight, 0, 10)
        Pace := Max(FloatSpeed, 0.05)
        Widgets.WBP_HexMapCode:
            MapName := Name
            MapCode := Code
            Scale := if (Size > 0.1) then Size else 1.0
            SizeX := Wide
            SizeXFrom := Wide - 0.02
            SizeY := Tall
            SizeYFrom := Tall - 0.02
            FloatOn := if (Rise > 0) then 0.0 else 1.0
            FloatFrom := (Max(Rise, 1) - 1) * 3.0
            FloatTo := Max(Rise, 1) * 3.0
            FloatSpeed := Pace
            WingMat := Look.Wing
            HexMat := Look.Hex
            BadgeMat := Look.Badge
            NameColor := Look.NameColor
            CodeColor := Look.CodeColor
            IconColor := Look.IconColor
            GlyphColor := Look.GlyphColor
            GlintColor := Look.GlintColor
            RainbowName := Look.RainbowName
            PlainName := logic{not Look.RainbowName?}

    Place(Bar : widget) : canvas =
        canvas:
            Slots := array:
                canvas_slot:
                    Anchors := anchors{ Minimum := vector2{ X := 0.0, Y := 0.0 }, Maximum := vector2{ X := 1.0, Y := 1.0 } }
                    Offsets := margin{ Left := OffsetX, Top := OffsetY, Right := -OffsetX, Bottom := -OffsetY }
                    Widget := Bar

    LookOf(Which : island_map_code_style) : island_map_code_look =
        case (Which):
            island_map_code_style.Rainbow => island_map_code_look:
                Wing := HexIslandCode.Materials.MI_HexCode_Rainbow_Wing{}
                Hex := HexIslandCode.Materials.MI_HexCode_Rainbow_Hex{}
                Badge := HexIslandCode.Materials.MI_HexCode_Rainbow_Badge{}
                IconColor := Tint("#FFFFFF")
                NameColor := Tint("#FFFFFF")
                CodeColor := Tint("#ECF1FF")
                GlyphColor := Tint("#FFFFFF")
                GlintColor := Tint("#FFFFFF")
                RainbowName := true
            island_map_code_style.Legendary => island_map_code_look:
                Wing := HexIslandCode.Materials.MI_HexCode_Legendary_Wing{}
                Hex := HexIslandCode.Materials.MI_HexCode_Legendary_Hex{}
                Badge := HexIslandCode.Materials.MI_HexCode_Legendary_Badge{}
                IconColor := Tint("#FFF1A6")
                NameColor := Tint("#FFF2C5")
                CodeColor := Tint("#FFFFFF")
                GlyphColor := Tint("#3A1203")
                GlintColor := Tint("#FFF6D0")
            island_map_code_style.OnyxGold => island_map_code_look:
                Wing := HexIslandCode.Materials.MI_HexCode_OnyxGold_Wing{}
                Hex := HexIslandCode.Materials.MI_HexCode_OnyxGold_Hex{}

files.name: LeaderboardManager.verse
files.code:
# LeaderboardManager.verse
# Summary: In-world UMG leaderboard (T-037). Ranks players by Prestige level/points and shows lifetime Kills/Gold/Diamonds and
#   Max Round Reached on one or more placed WBP_Leaderboard widget entities. Ranks live players plus a session-scoped snapshot of
#   players who left, so a long server session can still show a Top 10.
# Last modified: 2026-11-05 — v17 (T-102: award queues)
#
# Notes (still valid):
#  - Widget: real UMG WBP_Leaderboard placed as a 3D entity (GetSimulationEntity[].FindDescendantEntities + Verse-bindable fields; same
#    mechanism as LikeFavWorldUI). MULTIPLE placed entities are supported (all matches written each refresh). Placement in the Scene
#    Graph is an owner action; if none is placed the device logs a warning and does nothing. Row layout is explicit 10-row fields
#    per column (Rank, Name, Level, Kills, Gold, Diamonds, MaxRound); RowText carries only the name, rank goes to RankText1..10.
#  - Folder: this file must stay in custom_verse/LeaderboardLogic/ (the widget lives in LeaderboardLogic/Leaderboard/); a folder named
#    "Leaderboard" for the .verse file collided with the widget's module ("Ambiguous identifier"). As a sibling module the unqualified
#    Leaderboard.WBP_Leaderboard_entity reference resolves. If the widget class path changes, placed entity proxies must be recreated
#    (no MCP "repoint class" tool); current class: ...custom_verse-LeaderboardLogic-Leaderboard-WBP_Leaderboard_entity.
#  - Player names: a message built via "{Agent}" inside a <localizes> function renders lazily and is EMPTY once the player has left;
#    departed rows therefore store the generic DepartedPlayerNameMessage. `player` has no GetDisplayName and `message` is not comparable.
#  - Dedup: LeftPlayersSnapshots (plain in-memory array, not persistable, FIFO-capped at MaxLeftPlayerSnapshots) is deduplicated by
#    `player` identity (RemoveSnapshotForPlayer on join and before appending a new snapshot); it is the only way to keep a departed
#    player visible (persistent data of non-present players is not accessible).
#  - Data sources / independence: level/points and lifetime stats are read/written via PrestigeManager public getters
#    (GetLevel/GetPoints/GetKills/GetGoldEarned/GetDiamondsEarned/AddLifetimeStats) because the project is hard-capped at 4
#    persistent vars. Kills come from this module's own KillTrigger (bind to the SAME physical Trigger as GameManager's KillTrigger;
#    fires from GameManager's boss-defeat reward are ignored via GameManagerRef.IsBossRewardInProgress()). Gold/Diamonds come from
#    GameManager's public GoldAwardedEvent/DiamondsAwardedEvent; custom event() values do not support .Subscribe(), so a spawned loop
#    Awaits each. KNOWN LIMITATION: native Elimination Manager kill-time diamond drops never go through Verse and are not counted.
#  - Refresh: kill/gold/diamond events only increment a per-player in-memory PendingStats counter; the 5s RefreshLoop flushes them
#    with ONE batched AddLifetimeStats write per player, then refreshes (displayed = persistent + pending). CaptureLeavingPlayerSnapshot
#    flushes pending BEFORE snapshotting, then prunes via player_state_utils.WithRemovedKey. Join/leave/round-start refresh immediately.
#  - Max round: RoundStartTrigger (bind to the same physical Trigger as GameManager's) has only a ?agent payload, so
#    OnRoundStartTriggered reads GameManagerRef.GetCurrentRound() and calls UpdateMaxRoundReached for EVERY connected player
#    (the round is a run-wide fact); a disconnected player never gets later rounds ("reached while connected"). The column is
#    display-only; sort order is PrestigeLevel then PrestigePoints.
using { /Verse.org }
using { /Verse.org/Native }
using { /Verse.org/SceneGraph }
using { /Verse.org/Simulation }
using { /Fortnite.com/Devices }
using { /Fortnite.com/Game }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/UI }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/Diagnostics }
using { player_state_utils }

# T-070: not-yet-persisted lifetime deltas for one player, flushed by RefreshLoop in one write.
pending_stats := struct:
    Kills : int = 0
    Gold : int = 0
    Diamonds : int = 0

# A message built directly from an agent/player renders as that player's native display name -
# confirmed against an owner-supplied working example. Works for a LIVE agent only - it renders lazily,
# so do NOT store it for a departed player (it renders empty once the agent has left); departed rows use
# DepartedPlayerNameMessage() instead (T-071, see CaptureLeavingPlayerSnapshot).
AgentNameMessage<localizes>(Agent : agent) : message = "{Agent}"

# T-071: a "{Agent}" message renders lazily from the agent reference, so a snapshot of it renders
# EMPTY once that player has left the session. Owner decision (option b, 2026-09-29): departed
# players' rows show this generic localized label together with their frozen stats instead.
DepartedPlayerNameMessage<localizes>() : message = "Player left"

NameRowMessage<localizes>(NameMsg : message) : message = "{NameMsg}"

EmptyRowMessage<localizes>() : message = "---"

RankMessage<localizes>(RankText : string) : message = "{RankText}"

StatMessage<localizes>(Value : string) : message = "{Value}"

EmptyStatMessage<localizes>() : message = "---"

# One combined row, built fresh each refresh from either a live player or a frozen snapshot -
# NameMsg is already a fully-resolved message by the time this is built (see file header).
leaderboard_row := struct:
    NameMsg : message
    PrestigeLevel : int
    PrestigePoints : int
    Kills : int
    GoldEarned : int
    DiamondsEarned : int
    # v10 (T-037): MAXIMUM round reached while connected this run, NOT a cumulative total like
    # Kills/GoldEarned/DiamondsEarned above - see PrestigeManager.verse v10's
    # GetMaxRoundReached/UpdateMaxRoundReached header note for the exact semantics.
    MaxRoundReached : int

# Frozen copy of a departed player's stats (the name is the generic "Player left" label) - see file header's SESSION-SCOPED note.
session_leaderboard_entry := struct:
    # Kept for rejoin dedup (see RemoveSnapshotForPlayer) - `player` is comparable via `=` (it's
    # already used as a weak_map key elsewhere in this project, e.g. PrestigeManager.verse, which
    # requires a comparable key type) and, unlike the rendered NameMsg `message` (not comparable -
    # confirmed via a real BuildAll error), correctly resolves to the SAME value for the same
    # underlying account across a same-session leave/rejoin - this is a strictly better dedup key
    # than DisplayName text, not just a workaround for message not being comparable.
    Player : player
    NameMsg : message
    PrestigeLevel : int
    PrestigePoints : int
    Kills : int
    GoldEarned : int
    DiamondsEarned : int
    MaxRoundReached : int

leaderboard_manager := class(creative_device):

    # ============================================================
    # LOGGING (rule 2 - centralized logger, no direct Print() calls).
    # ============================================================
    @editable DebugLoggingEnabled : logic = true
    Log(LogMessage : string) : void=
        if (DebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Print(LogMessage)

    # Read-only access to GameManager's v24 public events and PrestigeManager's v7/v8 public
    # getters/setters - see file header. This module never calls into either beyond these plus the read-only GetCurrentRound/IsBossRewardInProgress getters;
    # neither of them ever calls into this module.
    @editable GameManagerRef : GameManager.game_manager = GameManager.game_manager{}
    @editable PrestigeManagerRef : PrestigeManager.prestige_manager = PrestigeManager.prestige_manager{}

    # Bind in UEFN to the SAME physical Trigger device already bound to GameManager's own
    # KillTrigger field - independent listener, not a reference to GameManager's field.
    @editable KillTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}

    # v10 (T-037 - MAX ROUND column): bind in UEFN to the SAME physical Trigger device already
    # bound to GameManager's own RoundStartTrigger field (T-038) - same independent-listener
    # pattern as KillTrigger above. RoundStartTrigger's payload is only `?agent` (whoever
    # triggered it, not the round number), so on fire this module reads the round number
    # independently via GameManagerRef.GetCurrentRound() (read-only getter, v29) rather than
    # GameManager exposing a new typed event for it - RoundStartTrigger already fires at exactly
    # the right moment (see GameManager.verse's own RoundStartTrigger field comment).
    @editable RoundStartTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}

    @editable RefreshIntervalSeconds : float = 5.0

    @editable MaxLeftPlayerSnapshots : int = 6

    var LeftPlayersSnapshots : []session_leaderboard_entry = array{}

    # T-070: per-player pending lifetime deltas (see file header v11).
    var PendingStats : [player]pending_stats = map{}

    GetPending(Player : player) : pending_stats=
        if (Existing := PendingStats[Player]):
            Existing
        else:
            pending_stats{}

    AddPending(Player : player, Kills : int, Gold : int, Diamonds : int) : void=
        Current := GetPending(Player)
        NewPending := pending_stats{Kills := Current.Kills + Kills, Gold := Current.Gold + Gold, Diamonds := Current.Diamonds + Diamonds}
        if (set PendingStats[Player] = NewPending) {}

    # One batched persistent write per player, then reset the pending counter.
    FlushPending(Player : player) : void=
        Current := GetPending(Player)
        if (Current.Kills > 0 or Current.Gold > 0 or Current.Diamonds > 0):
            PrestigeManagerRef.AddLifetimeStats(Player, Current.Kills, Current.Gold, Current.Diamonds)
            if (set PendingStats[Player] = pending_stats{}) {}

    FlushAllPending() : void=
        for (Player : GetPlayspace().GetPlayers()):
            FlushPending(Player)

    # Resolved once in OnBegin by finding EVERY placed WBP_Leaderboard 3D-prop entity in the Scene
    # Graph - see file header's PLACEMENT note. Supports placing more than one leaderboard prop in
    # the level (e.g. one near the lobby, one near an unlocked area); every found entity gets the
    # same rows written to it each refresh. Empty array if none were placed.
    var Widgets : []Leaderboard.WBP_Leaderboard_entity = array{}

    OnBegin<override>()<suspends> : void=
        if (SimEnt := GetSimulationEntity[]):
            set Widgets = for (Wid : SimEnt.FindDescendantEntities(Leaderboard.WBP_Leaderboard_entity)):
                Wid
        if (Widgets.Length > 0):
            Log("LeaderboardManager: OnBegin - found {Widgets.Length} placed WBP_Leaderboard entity/entities in the Scene Graph")
        else:
            Log("LeaderboardManager: WARNING - no WBP_Leaderboard entity found in the Scene Graph. Place the widget as a 3D prop in the level (same way WBP_LikeFavs is placed) or this device does nothing.")

        KillTrigger.TriggeredEvent.Subscribe(OnKillTriggered)
        RoundStartTrigger.TriggeredEvent.Subscribe(OnRoundStartTriggered)
        GetPlayspace().PlayerAddedEvent().Subscribe(OnPlayerAddedHandler)
        GetPlayspace().PlayerRemovedEvent().Subscribe(OnPlayerRemovedHandler)
        spawn:
            AwaitGoldAwardedLoop()
        spawn:
            AwaitDiamondsAwardedLoop()
        spawn:
            RefreshLoop()

    # --- Custom event await-loops (GameManager v24's GoldAwardedEvent/DiamondsAwardedEvent are
    # plain Verse `event()` values, which support `.Await()` but not `.Subscribe()`). ---
    AwaitGoldAwardedLoop()<suspends> : void=
        loop:
            # T-102: the event is only a wake-up (or a 1s fallback); the queue holds every award.
            race:
                block:
                    GameManagerRef.GoldAwardedEvent.Await()
                block:
                    Sleep(1.0)
            Awards := GameManagerRef.TakeLeaderboardGold()
            for (Payload : Awards):
                HandleGoldAwarded(Payload)

    AwaitDiamondsAwardedLoop()<suspends> : void=
        loop:
            race:
                block:
                    GameManagerRef.DiamondsAwardedEvent.Await()
                block:
                    Sleep(1.0)
            Awards := GameManagerRef.TakeLeaderboardDiamonds()
            for (Payload : Awards):
                HandleDiamondsAwarded(Payload)

    # T-091 instrumentation: handled counters, compared against GameManager's GoldSignalsSent/DiamondsSignalsSent.
    var GoldHandledCount : int = 0
    var DiamondsHandledCount : int = 0

    HandleGoldAwarded(Payload : tuple(agent, int)) : void=
        Agent := Payload(0)
        Amount := Payload(1)
        set GoldHandledCount += 1
        if (DebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Log("LeaderboardManager[SIGNAL-DIAG]: gold handled #{GoldHandledCount} / sent #{GameManagerRef.GoldSignalsSent} amount={Amount}")
        if (Player := player[Agent]):
            AddPending(Player, 0, Amount, 0)

    HandleDiamondsAwarded(Payload : tuple(agent, int)) : void=
        Agent := Payload(0)
        Amount := Payload(1)
        set DiamondsHandledCount += 1
        if (DebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Log("LeaderboardManager[SIGNAL-DIAG]: diamonds handled #{DiamondsHandledCount} / sent #{GameManagerRef.DiamondsSignalsSent} amount={Amount}")
        if (Player := player[Agent]):
            AddPending(Player, 0, 0, Amount)

    # trigger_device.TriggeredEvent's payload is `?agent` (optional) - confirmed via BuildAll.
    OnKillTriggered(MaybeAgent : ?agent) : void=
        if (Agent := MaybeAgent?):
            if (Player := player[Agent]):
                # T-079: the boss-defeat reward fires this same physical trigger for every player
                # (VFX hookup) - it is not a real kill, so it must not count.
                BossReward := GameManagerRef.IsBossRewardInProgress()
                if (BossReward?):
                    Log("LeaderboardManager: KillTrigger fired by the boss-defeat reward - not counted as a kill")
                else:
                    AddPending(Player, 1, 0, 0)

    # v10 (T-037 - MAX ROUND column): fired once per round start (see RoundStartTrigger field
    # comment above). The round is shared/global for the whole run, so on every fire this updates
    # EVERY CURRENTLY CONNECTED player's max, not just whoever's `?agent` payload triggered it
    # (multiplayer: the round advancing isn't any one player's individual action). A player who
    # disconnected before this round simply isn't in GetPlayspace().GetPlayers() any more and
    # never receives the update for it - exactly the "reached while connected" semantics the
    # owner asked for (see PrestigeManager.verse v10's UpdateMaxRoundReached header note).
    OnRoundStartTriggered(MaybeAgent : ?agent) : void=
        CurrentRound := GameManagerRef.GetCurrentRound()
        for (Player : GetPlayspace().GetPlayers()):
            PrestigeManagerRef.UpdateMaxRoundReached(Player, CurrentRound)
        Log("LeaderboardManager: round {CurrentRound} started - updated MaxRoundReached for all connected players")
        spawn:
            RefreshLeaderboardDisplay()

    # --- Player join/leave ---
    # BUG FIX (2026-09-13, owner report): a player who left and rejoined the SAME server session
    # showed up TWICE in the Top 10 - their stale LeftPlayersSnapshots entry (from the earlier
    # leave) kept coexisting with their new LIVE row, because nothing ever removed the old
    # snapshot on rejoin. RemoveSnapshotForPlayer() below is the dedup-by-`player`-identity step
    # (called on join and before each new snapshot).
    OnPlayerAddedHandler(Player : player) : void=
        spawn:
            RemoveSnapshotByNameThenRefresh(Player)

    RemoveSnapshotByNameThenRefresh(Player : player)<suspends> : void=
        RemoveSnapshotForPlayer(Player)
        RefreshLeaderboardDisplay()

    OnPlayerRemovedHandler(Player : player) : void=
        spawn:
            CaptureLeavingPlayerSnapshot(Player)

    # Removes any existing LeftPlayersSnapshots entry captured for this same player (identity
    # comparison on the `player` value itself - see session_leaderboard_entry.Player comment).
    # Used both when a player rejoins (their old snapshot must not coexist with their new live row)
    # and defensively before adding a fresh snapshot on a repeat leave, so a stale duplicate can
    # never linger for the same player across a leave/rejoin/leave sequence.
    RemoveSnapshotForPlayer(Player : player) : void=
        set LeftPlayersSnapshots = for (Entry : LeftPlayersSnapshots, Entry.Player <> Player):
            Entry

    CaptureLeavingPlayerSnapshot(Player : player)<suspends> : void=
        # Defensive: remove any stale snapshot left over for this same player BEFORE adding the
        # fresh one, so a leave/rejoin/leave-again sequence can never produce two entries.
        RemoveSnapshotForPlayer(Player)
        # T-070: persist this player's pending counters before reading them back, then prune.
        FlushPending(Player)
        if (NewPendingMap := PendingStats.WithRemovedKey(Player)?):
            set PendingStats = NewPendingMap
        NewEntry := session_leaderboard_entry{
            Player := Player
            NameMsg := DepartedPlayerNameMessage()
            PrestigeLevel := PrestigeManagerRef.GetLevel(Player)
            PrestigePoints := PrestigeManagerRef.GetPoints(Player)
            Kills := PrestigeManagerRef.GetKills(Player)
            GoldEarned := PrestigeManagerRef.GetGoldEarned(Player)
            DiamondsEarned := PrestigeManagerRef.GetDiamondsEarned(Player)
            MaxRoundReached := PrestigeManagerRef.GetMaxRoundReached(Player)
        }
        set LeftPlayersSnapshots += array{NewEntry}
        # FIFO cap - see MaxLeftPlayerSnapshots field comment.
        if (LeftPlayersSnapshots.Length > MaxLeftPlayerSnapshots):
            if (Trimmed := LeftPlayersSnapshots.RemoveElement[0]):
                set LeftPlayersSnapshots = Trimmed
        Log("LeaderboardManager: snapshotted a departing player into the session leaderboard")
        RefreshLeaderboardDisplay()

    # --- Ranking + display ---
    RefreshLoop()<suspends> : void=
        loop:
            FlushAllPending()
            RefreshLeaderboardDisplay()
            Sleep(RefreshIntervalSeconds)

    RefreshLeaderboardDisplay()<suspends> : void=
        if (Widgets.Length > 0):
            var Rows : []leaderboard_row = array{}
            for (Player : GetPlayspace().GetPlayers()):
                Pending := GetPending(Player)
                NewRow := leaderboard_row{
                    NameMsg := AgentNameMessage(Player)
                    PrestigeLevel := PrestigeManagerRef.GetLevel(Player)
                    PrestigePoints := PrestigeManagerRef.GetPoints(Player)
                    Kills := PrestigeManagerRef.GetKills(Player) + Pending.Kills
                    GoldEarned := PrestigeManagerRef.GetGoldEarned(Player) + Pending.Gold
                    DiamondsEarned := PrestigeManagerRef.GetDiamondsEarned(Player) + Pending.Diamonds
                    MaxRoundReached := PrestigeManagerRef.GetMaxRoundReached(Player)
                }
                set Rows += array{NewRow}
            for (Entry : LeftPlayersSnapshots):
                SnapshotRow := leaderboard_row{
                    NameMsg := Entry.NameMsg
                    PrestigeLevel := Entry.PrestigeLevel
                    PrestigePoints := Entry.PrestigePoints
                    Kills := Entry.Kills
                    GoldEarned := Entry.GoldEarned
                    DiamondsEarned := Entry.DiamondsEarned
                    MaxRoundReached := Entry.MaxRoundReached
                }
                set Rows += array{SnapshotRow}

            SortedRows := SortRowsDescendingByPrestige(Rows)
            for (Widget : Widgets):
                WriteWidgetRows(Widget, SortedRows)

    # Small selection sort (N is at most a handful of players + snapshots - no need for anything
    # fancier). Descending by PrestigeLevel, then PrestigePoints as a tiebreaker.
    SortRowsDescendingByPrestige(Rows : []leaderboard_row) : []leaderboard_row=
        var Remaining : []leaderboard_row = Rows
        var Sorted : []leaderboard_row = array{}
        loop:
            if (Remaining.Length = 0):
                break
            if (FirstRow := Remaining[0]):
                var BestIndex : int = 0
                var BestRow : leaderboard_row = FirstRow
                for (Index -> Row : Remaining):
                    IsBetter := IsRowHigherRanked(Row, BestRow)
                    if (IsBetter?):
                        set BestIndex = Index
                        set BestRow = Row
                set Sorted += array{BestRow}
                if (NewRemaining := Remaining.RemoveElement[BestIndex]):
                    set Remaining = NewRemaining
                else:
                    set Remaining = array{}
            else:
                break
        Sorted

    IsRowHigherRanked(Candidate : leaderboard_row, Current : leaderboard_row) : logic=
        if (Candidate.PrestigeLevel > Current.PrestigeLevel):
            true
        else if (Candidate.PrestigeLevel < Current.PrestigeLevel):
            false
        else if (Candidate.PrestigePoints > Current.PrestigePoints):
            true
        else:
            false

    # Writes up to 10 rows across 7 REAL separate widget fields per row (Rank, Name, Level, Kills,
    # Gold, Diamonds, MaxRound) - not one combined string - per owner's explicit correction ("campi
    # separati per riga (vera tabella)"). Verse has no way to loop over a fixed set of
    # differently-named fields dynamically, so this is spelled out explicitly per row (same shape
    # SetWidgetSlotData uses in daily_quests_device.verse).
    WriteWidgetRows(Widget : Leaderboard.WBP_Leaderboard_entity, SortedRows : []leaderboard_row) : void=
        set Widget.RankText1 = RankMessage("1")
        set Widget.RankText2 = RankMessage("2")
        set Widget.RankText3 = RankMessage("3")
        set Widget.RankText4 = RankMessage("4")
        set Widget.RankText5 = RankMessage("5")
        set Widget.RankText6 = RankMessage("6")
        set Widget.RankText7 = RankMessage("7")
        set Widget.RankText8 = RankMessage("8")
        set Widget.RankText9 = RankMessage("9")
        set Widget.RankText10 = RankMessage("10")

        set Widget.RowText1 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 0)
        set Widget.RowText2 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 1)
        set Widget.RowText3 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 2)
        set Widget.RowText4 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 3)
        set Widget.RowText5 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 4)
        set Widget.RowText6 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 5)
        set Widget.RowText7 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 6)
        set Widget.RowText8 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 7)
        set Widget.RowText9 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 8)
        set Widget.RowText10 = BuildNameMessage(SortedRows, 9)

        set Widget.LevelText1 = BuildStatMessage(SortedRows, 0, LevelStat)
        set Widget.LevelText2 = BuildStatMessage(SortedRows, 1, LevelStat)
        set Widget.LevelText3 = BuildStatMessage(SortedRows, 2, LevelStat)
        set Widget.LevelText4 = BuildStatMessage(SortedRows, 3, LevelStat)
        set Widget.LevelText5 = BuildStatMessage(SortedRows, 4, LevelStat)
        set Widget.LevelText6 = BuildStatMessage(SortedRows, 5, LevelStat)
        set Widget.LevelText7 = BuildStatMessage(SortedRows, 6, LevelStat)

    # Which stat column to read - internal tags (not user-facing), avoids duplicating
    # BuildStatMessage per column.
    LevelStat : string = "Level"
    KillsStat : string = "Kills"
    GoldStat : string = "Gold"
    DiamondsStat : string = "Diamonds"

    BuildStatMessage(SortedRows : []leaderboard_row, RowIndex : int, StatKind : string) : message=

            else if (StatKind = "Diamonds"):
                StatMessage("{Row.DiamondsEarned}")
            else:
                StatMessage("{Row.MaxRoundReached}")
        else:
            EmptyStatMessage()
