files.name: PrestigeManager.verse
files.code:
# PrestigeManager.verse
# Summary: Standalone per-player, uncapped "prestige/level" module (T-014). Owner-configured @editable
#   ScoreEvents (Points + []trigger_device each) award prestige points; level thresholds grow
#   exponentially (LevelTargetMultiplier); level/progress are pushed to WB_Main; state persists via a
#   <persistable> weak_map that also stores leaderboard stats, area unlocks, VIP flag and upgrade levels.
# Last modified: 2026-11-05 — v31
#
#
# Notes (still valid):
#  - Score events: same class<concrete> + single top-level array shape as CurrencyUIAnimation's currency_category
#    (T-027/T-028); add/remove events/triggers in the Details panel without Verse changes. Whichever trigger in an
#    event's array fires, the activating player gets that event's Points.
#  - Level formula: Threshold(Level) = Round(BasePointsPerLevel * LevelTargetMultiplier ^ (Level-1)) via an iterative
#    loop (no native float Pow with int exponent). Level starts at 1, no cap; excess points carry over and one big
#    award can level up several times. Simple per-player counter, so no state machine (rule 5) was judged needed.
#  - Independence: never calls into GameManager. It subscribes to the same native triggers GameManager uses. The only
#    shared piece is the WB_Main widget, read via coin_display_manager.GetWidget through an @editable game_manager ref
#    (a second WB_Main instance was rejected: it would duplicate the whole HUD).
#  - Multiplayer: PlayerPoints/PlayerLevel are [player]int maps (never shared counters). WB_Main fields written:
#    Prestige (message), Prestige_progress (float 0-1), Value, TargetValue (message), Prestige_icon (texture).
#  - Persistence: module-scoped weak_map(player, prestige_persistent_data). Islands are hard-capped at 4 module-scoped
#    persistent vars (confirmed by compile error) and all 4 are used, so this ONE class carries every persisted field
#    (Kills/GoldEarned/DiamondsEarned/MaxRoundReached, UnlockedAreaIndices, HasVipPermanent, UpgradeLevel*). A
#    persistable class literal resets any field not mentioned, so writes go through CopyPrestigeData. Public
#    getters/setters are pure storage delegates; this module never calls AreaUnlock/UpgradeManager.
#  - MaxRoundReached is a maximum (only written when strictly higher); callers invoke it per round-start for players
#    connected at that moment.
#  - VIP: PrestigeManager -> VipPack is the ONLY cross-module type reference (a reverse reference made a package
#    cycle that halted compilation, v14). VipGrantTrigger is shared with Vip_Manager; the hidden test button must NOT
#    persist VIP, so OnVipGrantTriggered persists only when PlayerLevel >= VipPrestigeLevelThreshold (B-030). VIP is
#    removed below the threshold and re-applied on the upward crossing; a persisted flag is re-pushed on rejoin.
#    RefreshWidget always writes Prestige_icon (VipPrestigeIcon if VIP, else DefaultPrestigeIcon if configured).
#  - Aura (T-068/T-088): AuraThresholds is a []prestige_aura_threshold (LevelThreshold + AuraTrigger). The target aura is
#    computed directly from the level (highest threshold <= level) on level change and on join/rejoin, with
#    AuraCleanupTrigger fired first; 8 levels (5;10;20;25;30;40;50;75), config-driven. The Trigger->Powerup wiring is
#    manual in UEFN, and class-array element fields cannot be populated via MCP (same limit as ScoreEvents/
#    CurrencyCategories) - the owner fills them in the Details panel.
#  - Rounding: base Verse Floor truncates, so RoundFloatToInt (shared_utils) uses Floor(x+0.5); inputs are non-negative.
using { /Fortnite.com/Devices }
using { /Verse.org/Simulation }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/Diagnostics }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/UI }
using { big_number_utils }
using { VipPack }
using { /Verse.org/Assets }
using { player_state_utils }
using { shared_utils }

# --- v5: native Verse persistent storage (replaces PointsTracker/LevelTracker) ---
# Must be <final><persistable>, no superclass, every member itself persistable (int qualifies).
# Version field kept per Epic's own convention for this pattern, in case a later change needs to
# distinguish old vs. new saved shapes (new fields on a class are safe to add post-publish with
# defaults - see file header).
prestige_persistent_data := class<final><persistable>:
    Version : int = 1
    Points : int = 0
    Level : int = 1
    # v8 (2026-09-11, T-037 - leaderboard): lifetime Kills/Gold/Diamonds live HERE, reusing this
    # SAME persistable class/weak_map, instead of LeaderboardManager.verse having its own -
    # Fortnite islands are hard-capped at 4 module-scoped persistent `var`s total project-wide
    # (confirmed by a real BuildAll error: "Only 4 persistent vars allowed" - this project already
    # has exactly 4: this one, DailyQuests, DailyRewards, PinPad). New fields on a class are safe
    # to add post-publish with defaults (see file header), so this is the only way to add a 5th
    # tracked stat set without exceeding the cap. These three are NEVER decremented by spending -
    # deliberately different numbers from GameManager.verse's PlayerGold/PlayerDiamonds (spendable
    # balances that go down).
    Kills : int = 0
    GoldEarned : int = 0
    DiamondsEarned : int = 0
    # v9 (2026-09-12, T-040): AreaUnlockManager.verse's unlocked-area indices, reusing THIS
    # SAME persistable class/weak_map for the identical reason as the T-037 leaderboard stats
    # above - the project is already at the hard 4-persistent-var-per-project cap (PrestigeManager,
    # DailyQuests, DailyRewards, PinPad), so a 5th weak_map for area-unlock state would fail to
    # compile. See GetUnlockedAreaIndices/SetUnlockedAreaIndices below and
    # AreaUnlockManager.verse v17's header note for the full migration rationale (replacing that
    # module's Tracker-Device-backed persistence, B-012's root cause, with this weak_map).
    UnlockedAreaIndices : []int = array{}
    # v10 (2026-09-13, T-037 - leaderboard MAX ROUND column): MaxRoundReached is a MAXIMUM,
    # not a cumulative total like Kills/GoldEarned/DiamondsEarned above - the highest round
    # number this player was connected for during any run. See GetMaxRoundReached/
    # UpdateMaxRoundReached below for the write-only-if-higher semantics. Reusing this SAME
    # persistable class/weak_map for the identical reason as every other T-037/T-040 addition
    # above - the project is hard-capped at 4 module-scoped persistent `var`s total.
    MaxRoundReached : int = 0
    # v13 (2026-09-19, T-063): single persisted source of truth for "does this player have VIP".
    # Written by this module (SetHasVip from ApplyLevelUps on the prestige-100 crossing, and from
    # OnVipGrantTriggered when the shared VipGrantTrigger fires at/above the threshold); read back on rejoin in
    # OnPlayerAdded and pushed to Vip_Manager via VipManagerRef.ApplyVipOwnership. Reusing this SAME persistable class/weak_map for
    # the identical hard-4-persistent-var-cap reason as every other addition above.
    HasVipPermanent : logic = false
    # v19 (2026-09-28, T-069): per-category permanent upgrade levels for UpgradeManager.verse,
    # reusing THIS SAME persistable class/weak_map for the identical hard-4-persistent-var-cap
    # reason as every other addition above (PrestigeManager/DailyQuests/DailyRewards/PinPad
    # already occupy all 4 slots project-wide). 0 means "no level purchased yet" for that
    # category (0-based count of levels owned == index of the next purchasable level in that
    # category's @editable levels array). See GetShieldLevel/SetShieldLevel and the matching
    # Health/Speed/Damage pairs below - pure storage delegate, same as UnlockedAreaIndices.
    UpgradeLevelShield : int = 0
    UpgradeLevelHealth : int = 0
    UpgradeLevelSpeed : int = 0
    UpgradeLevelDamage : int = 0

# Module-scoped weak_map(player, T) - Epic's persistence system auto-loads each player's
# previously saved entry into this map when they join, and a plain `set` write persists it
# immediately (no explicit Save()/Load() calls needed, unlike Tracker Device).
var PrestigeData : weak_map(player, prestige_persistent_data) = map{}

# v8 (T-037): shared read/write helpers so every write-site (PersistPrestige and the new
# lifetime-stat setters below) always carries ALL fields forward - a persistable class has no
# struct-style "copy with one field changed" shortcut, so every `set PrestigeData[Player] = ...`
# must construct the full object explicitly or it would silently reset whichever fields it
# doesn't mention back to their defaults.
# T-075: the ONE place that copies all 12 persistent fields. Every write-site used to spell out the
# full 12-field constructor (12 copies); now they call CopyPrestigeData(Base, ?Field := option{New}...)
# naming only the fields they change - every field not named is carried over from Base, so a field
# added to prestige_persistent_data only has to be added here (and to the class), never forgotten at
# a call site.
CopyPrestigeData(Base : prestige_persistent_data, ?Points : ?int = false, ?Level : ?int = false, ?Kills : ?int = false, ?GoldEarned : ?int = false, ?DiamondsEarned : ?int = false, ?UnlockedAreaIndices : ?[]int = false, ?MaxRoundReached : ?int = false, ?HasVipPermanent : ?logic = false, ?UpgradeLevelShield : ?int = false, ?UpgradeLevelHealth : ?int = false, ?UpgradeLevelSpeed : ?int = false, ?UpgradeLevelDamage : ?int = false) : prestige_persistent_data=
    prestige_persistent_data{
        Points := if (V := Points?) then V else Base.Points
        Level := if (V := Level?) then V else Base.Level
        Kills := if (V := Kills?) then V else Base.Kills
        GoldEarned := if (V := GoldEarned?) then V else Base.GoldEarned
        DiamondsEarned := if (V := DiamondsEarned?) then V else Base.DiamondsEarned
        UnlockedAreaIndices := if (V := UnlockedAreaIndices?) then V else Base.UnlockedAreaIndices
        MaxRoundReached := if (V := MaxRoundReached?) then V else Base.MaxRoundReached
        HasVipPermanent := if (V := HasVipPermanent?) then V else Base.HasVipPermanent
        UpgradeLevelShield := if (V := UpgradeLevelShield?) then V else Base.UpgradeLevelShield
        UpgradeLevelHealth := if (V := UpgradeLevelHealth?) then V else Base.UpgradeLevelHealth
        UpgradeLevelSpeed := if (V := UpgradeLevelSpeed?) then V else Base.UpgradeLevelSpeed
        UpgradeLevelDamage := if (V := UpgradeLevelDamage?) then V else Base.UpgradeLevelDamage
    }

GetPersistentSnapshot(Player : player)<transacts> : prestige_persistent_data=
    if (Existing := PrestigeData[Player]):
        Existing
    else:
        prestige_persistent_data{}

WritePersistentSnapshot(Player : player, Snapshot : prestige_persistent_data) : void=
    if (FitsInPlayerMap[Snapshot]):
        if (set PrestigeData[Player] = Snapshot) {}

# --- Float -> int rounding note (originally for PointsMultiplier, T-034; RoundFloatToInt now lives in shared_utils and is used by LevelThreshold) ---
# Base Verse's Floor() truncates toward zero; this project's point rewards are always
# non-negative (Points:int >= 0 on every score_event, enforced by SubscribeScoreEvent's own
# "Points <= 0 skipped" check), so a simple +0.5 half-up bias is correct and documented here
# rather than reusing Floor's truncation silently and under-awarding fractional multipliers.
# (T-080: the RoundFloatToInt implementation itself now lives in the shared shared_utils module.)

# --- Prestige level text formatting (single swap-point, same convention as
# coin_display_manager.verse's RoundToMessage) ---
PrestigeLevelToMessage<localizes>(Value : string) : message = "Lvl {Value}"

# --- T-035: plain-number text formatting for WB_Main's Value/TargetValue fields (exact field
# names confirmed live via MCP VerseFieldsToolset.ListVerseFields before writing this change —
# both are `message` type on WB_Main, not int/float, so they need the same
# int->string->message swap-point pattern as PrestigeLevelToMessage above, just without the
# "Lvl " prefix). ---
PlainNumberToMessage<localizes>(Value : string) : message = "{Value}"

# --- Score event: one Points reward + one arbitrarily-expandable trigger array (T-014,
# mirrors currency_category from CurrencyUIAnimation.verse T-028 v7 exactly: class<concrete>,
# NOT a struct, so the Triggers sub-array is independently expandable in the Details panel).
# Any trigger in Triggers firing awards Points to the activating player. The owner populates a
# single @editable []score_event array (ScoreEvents below) with as many events as needed
# directly in UEFN — no fixed/named slots, no Verse change required to add one. ---
score_event := class<concrete>:
    @editable
    Points : int = 0

    @editable
    Triggers : []trigger_device = array{}

# (Applies to score_event_listener below, not to prestige_aura_threshold.) Per-trigger Subscribe target: Verse doesn't support a locally-scoped named function or a bare
# lambda literal inside a for-loop body, so each trigger gets one small listener object that
# remembers which manager + how many points it's responsible for (same shape as
# currency_trigger_listener in CurrencyUIAnimation.verse).
# --- T-068: one permanent prestige-aura threshold. class<concrete> (not a struct) so the array
# stays independently expandable in the Details panel with zero Verse changes, same reasoning as
# score_event above. AuraTrigger is the dedicated Trigger Device fired once per crossing/rejoin
# for this specific threshold - the owner wires that Trigger's own TriggeredEvent, manually in
# UEFN's native device graph, to the matching already-placed Powerup Device (1:1 mapping, T-068
# owner clarification). This module never references a Powerup Device directly. ---
prestige_aura_threshold := class<concrete>:
    @editable
    LevelThreshold : int = 0

    @editable
    AuraTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}

score_event_listener := class:
    Manager : prestige_manager
    Points : int

    OnTriggered(MaybeAgent : ?agent) : void =
        if (Agent := MaybeAgent?):
            Manager.AwardPoints(Agent, Points)

prestige_manager<public> := class(creative_device):

    # --- Logging (rule 2 — centralized logger, no direct Print() calls) ---
    @editable DebugLoggingEnabled : logic = false
    Log(LogMessage : string) : void=
        if (DebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Print(LogMessage)

    # --- Score events (T-014 point 2): single arbitrary-length array of score_event class
    # instances, each with its own Points and its own expandable Triggers array. Populate
    # directly in the Details panel — no fixed count, no Verse change needed to add another. ---
    @editable
    ScoreEvents : []score_event = array{}

    # --- T-088 (v25): aura config + direct target-aura computation (replaces v17's per-threshold
    # FireAuraTriggersForRange and v18's B-031 Sleep(2.0) diagnostic, both removed). The aura a player
    # should wear is computed DIRECTLY from their level: the configured AuraThresholds entry with the
    # highest LevelThreshold <= level (none if the level is below the lowest threshold). No iteration
    # over all levels, no individual aura on/off: this module only fires AuraCleanupTrigger (the owner's
    # trigger graph clears every aura) and then the ONE AuraTrigger of the target aura.
    # Returns the index into AuraThresholds of the target aura for Level, or -1 for "no aura".
    # Entries with LevelThreshold <= 0 are unset and ignored.
    FindTargetAuraIndex(Level : int) : int=
        var BestIndex : int = -1
        var BestThreshold : int = 0
        for (Index -> Entry : AuraThresholds):
            if (Entry.LevelThreshold > 0, Entry.LevelThreshold <= Level, Entry.LevelThreshold > BestThreshold):
                set BestThreshold = Entry.LevelThreshold
                set BestIndex = Index
        BestIndex

    # Logs (explicitly) every AuraThresholds entry that is empty/unset, so a misconfigured Details panel is visible.
    LogEmptyAuraEntries() : void=
        if (AuraThresholds.Length = 0):
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] AuraThresholds is EMPTY - no aura will ever be assigned (configure it in the Details panel)")
        for (Index -> Entry : AuraThresholds):
            if (Entry.LevelThreshold <= 0):
                Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] AuraThresholds[{Index}] is empty/unset (LevelThreshold <= 0) - ignored")

    # Applies the aura for NewLevel to Player. OldLevel = the level before the change, or 0 on join/rejoin
    # (join always applies). On a level change whose target aura is unchanged, nothing is re-fired (cleanup
    # would only make the VFX flicker). Per-player only: Player is the one whose level changed.
    ApplyAuraForLevel(Player : player, OldLevel : int, NewLevel : int, Reason : string) : void=
        LogEmptyAuraEntries()
        TargetIndex := FindTargetAuraIndex(NewLevel)
        OldIndex := if (OldLevel > 0) then FindTargetAuraIndex(OldLevel) else -2
        if (TargetIndex = OldIndex):
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] aura ({Reason}): level {OldLevel} -> {NewLevel}, target aura unchanged (index {TargetIndex}) - nothing fired")
            return
        if (TargetIndex < 0, OldLevel <= 0):
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] aura ({Reason}): level {NewLevel} is below the lowest threshold and there is no previous aura - nothing to clean, nothing fired")
            return
        if (Entry := AuraThresholds[TargetIndex]):
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] aura ({Reason}): level {NewLevel} -> target aura index {TargetIndex}, threshold {Entry.LevelThreshold}")
        else:
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] aura ({Reason}): level {NewLevel} is below the lowest threshold -> NO target aura (cleanup only)")
        AuraCleanupTrigger.Trigger(Player)
        Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] aura cleanup trigger fired (before assigning the new aura)")
        if (Entry := AuraThresholds[TargetIndex]):
            Entry.AuraTrigger.Trigger(Player)
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] aura trigger fired for threshold {Entry.LevelThreshold} (index {TargetIndex})")

    # T-088 (v25, business logic): VIP must follow the level crossing in BOTH directions. A DROP below
    # VipPrestigeLevelThreshold removes the persisted VIP flag and the live VIP state (barriers/VFX) via
    # Vip_Manager.ApplyVipOwnership(false). (The upward crossing is handled in ApplyLevelUps.)
    SyncVipAfterLevelDrop(Player : player, OldLevel : int, NewLevel : int) : void=
        if (OldLevel >= VipPrestigeLevelThreshold, NewLevel < VipPrestigeLevelThreshold):
            SetHasVip(Player, false)
            VipManagerRef.ApplyVipOwnership(Player, false)
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] player dropped below the VIP prestige threshold ({OldLevel} -> {NewLevel}) - persisted VIP flag cleared and live VIP removed")

    # --- T-088 (v25): DEBUG-ONLY level triggers. Subscribed only when DebugTriggersEnabled is true.
    # UP awards exactly the points missing to the next level through the normal AwardPoints path (same
    # effects as a natural level-up). DOWN lowers the level by 1 (minimum 1), zeroes the points, persists,
    # re-evaluates VIP/aura and refreshes the widget. Per-player (the activating player only). ---
    OnDebugLevelUp(MaybeAgent : ?agent) : void=
        if (Agent := MaybeAgent?, Player := player[Agent]):
            CurrentLevel := if (L := PlayerLevel[Player]) then L else 1
            CurrentPoints := if (P := PlayerPoints[Player]) then P else 0
            Missing := LevelThreshold(CurrentLevel) - CurrentPoints
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] DEBUG UP pressed - level {CurrentLevel}, {CurrentPoints} pts, missing {Missing} pts to the next level")
            if (Missing > 0):
                AwardPoints(Player, Missing)
            else:
                Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] DEBUG UP - nothing missing (threshold <= 0 or already met), ignored")

    OnDebugLevelDown(MaybeAgent : ?agent) : void=
        if (Agent := MaybeAgent?, Player := player[Agent]):
            OldLevel := if (L := PlayerLevel[Player]) then L else 1
            if (OldLevel <= 1):
                Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] DEBUG DOWN pressed at level 1 - minimum level, no-op")
                return
            NewLevel := OldLevel - 1
            if (set PlayerLevel[Player] = NewLevel, set PlayerPoints[Player] = 0):
                Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] DEBUG DOWN - level {OldLevel} -> {NewLevel}, points reset to 0")
                SyncVipAfterLevelDrop(Player, OldLevel, NewLevel)
                ApplyAuraForLevel(Player, OldLevel, NewLevel, "debug DOWN")
                PersistPrestige(Player)
                RefreshWidget(Player)

    # Threshold(Level) = Round(BasePointsPerLevel * LevelTargetMultiplier ^ (Level - 1)).
    # LevelTargetMultiplier scales the TARGET required for the next level, exponentially per
    # level — this is the field the owner actually asked for (was wrongly implemented as a
    # points-earned multiplier in v2/v3, see header). Level itself is never capped.
    @editable BasePointsPerLevel : int = 100
    @editable LevelTargetMultiplier : float = 1.1

    # --- Level-up notification (v6, 2026-09-11) ---
    # Fired once per level gained (see ApplyLevelUps) - bind its TriggeredEvent, in the UEFN
    # device graph, to whatever should react to a prestige level-up (an XP reward via an
    # Accolade Device, another system that further boosts prestige, etc.) - same native
    # Trigger-as-output pattern already used by AreaUnlockManager.verse's UnlockTrigger and
    # (removed shop_device.verse reference - that file no longer exists). This module only fires it - what it's wired
    # to is entirely the owner's UEFN device-graph configuration, not Verse code here.
    @editable LevelUpTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}

    # --- T-053 (2026-09-18): VIP-via-Prestige bypass (Epic policy compliance) ---
    # Shared native trigger_device, the SAME one PrestigeManager and the hidden debug button both fire (bind
    # this @editable slot in the UEFN Details panel to the same placed trigger_device actor as
    # Vip_Manager.verse's VipGrantTrigger - see Vip_Manager.verse's v3 header for the full rationale). Fired once,
    # VipGrantTriggerRef - see Vip_Manager.verse's v3 header for the full rationale). Fired once,
    # from ApplyLevelUps below, the moment a player's LEVEL crosses VipPrestigeLevelThreshold -
    # this module never applies VIP barriers/VFX/bonus itself (independence pattern, same as
    # coin_display_manager - see project memory feedback_coin_display_manager_independence.md), it
    # signals the crossing, persists the VIP flag itself (SetHasVip) and also listens to this trigger (OnVipGrantTriggered).
    @editable VipGrantTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}
    @editable VipPrestigeLevelThreshold : int = 100

    # --- T-054 (2026-09-18): VIP icon override on WB_Main ---
    # Device-ref to the SAME placed Vip_Manager instance (bind in the Details panel to the same
    # actor as VipGrantTrigger's counterpart above) - used for PlayerHasVip (icon selection) and for pushing
    # the persisted flag via ApplyVipOwnership on join; VIP sources are the prestige-100 crossing and the hidden debug button, as one
    # unified status. VipPrestigeIcon is the texture written into WB_Main's Prestige_icon field
    # when the player has VIP; when they do not, DefaultPrestigeIcon is written (if configured), otherwise
    # the Widget Blueprint's own default icon shows.
    @editable VipManagerRef : VipPack.Vip_Manager = VipPack.Vip_Manager{}

    # Optional, same "no bogus placeholder asset" pattern already used by CurrencyUIAnimation.
    # verse's `Icon : ?material = false` - avoids inventing a fake default texture literal;
    # yet", falls through to the DefaultPrestigeIcon branch (written if configured) like VIP=false below.
    # (see RefreshWidget)
    @editable VipPrestigeIcon : ?texture = false

    # v16 (B-030 fix): "normal" prestige icon, written whenever the player does NOT have VIP -
    # same "no bogus placeholder asset" pattern as VipPrestigeIcon above. Closes the asymmetry
    # where the non-VIP branch never wrote Widget.Prestige_icon at all, leaving a stale value
    # from whatever the Widget Blueprint's own default was or a previous session/refresh left
    # behind (B-030). Unset means "no default icon configured yet" - nothing is written, same
    # as an unset VipPrestigeIcon today.
    @editable DefaultPrestigeIcon : ?texture = false

    # --- Shared WB_Main access (T-014 point 4 / independence note above) ---
    # Reference to the SAME placed game_manager device instance whose (now-public) CoinDisplay
    # owns the per-player WB_Main widgets. Read-only access via GameManager.CoinDisplay.GetWidget
    # — this module never calls any other GameManager method and GameManager never calls this one.
    @editable GameManagerRef : GameManager.game_manager = GameManager.game_manager{}

    # --- T-068 (2026-09-27): permanent prestige-aura thresholds ---
    # One dedicated Trigger Device per threshold - 8 aura levels (owner: 5;10;20;25;30;40;50;75;
    # earlier notes said 9, which was wrong), 1:1 with the already-placed Powerup Devices. The levels
    # live ONLY in this array (config-driven, nothing hardcoded in Verse): populate each element's
    # LevelThreshold + AuraTrigger in the Details panel; any count works with no Verse change. This
    # module only ever fires AuraCleanupTrigger and then ONE AuraTrigger.Trigger(Player); the
    # Trigger->Powerup wiring that applies the Niagara aura is done manually by the owner in UEFN's
    # native device graph, never by this file.
    @editable
    AuraThresholds : []prestige_aura_threshold = array{}

    # T-088 (v25): fired (with the affected player) BEFORE a new aura is assigned - the owner's trigger
    # graph wires it so that it clears every aura VFX/powerup. This module never disables auras one by one.
    @editable AuraCleanupTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}

    # T-088 (v25): TEST-ONLY debug level triggers. Do nothing unless DebugTriggersEnabled is true (default
    # false - leave it false in production builds).
    @editable DebugTriggersEnabled : logic = false
    @editable DebugLevelUpTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}
    @editable DebugLevelDownTrigger : trigger_device = trigger_device{}

    # --- Per-player state (rule 3 — multiplayer-safe, never global) ---
    var PlayerPoints : [player]int = map{}
    var PlayerLevel : [player]int = map{}

    # v7 (2026-09-11, T-037 - leaderboard): public read-only getters, same "expose a getter,
    # don't reach in" pattern already established by GameManager.CoinDisplay.GetWidget - lets an
    # independent module (LeaderboardManager.verse) read a player's current level/points without
    # this module calling out to anything or exposing the maps themselves.
    GetLevel<public>(Player : player)<transacts> : int=
        if (Level := PlayerLevel[Player]):
            Level
        else:
            # v21 (T-073): the session cache is pruned on leave, so fall back to the persisted
            # value (PersistPrestige writes it on every award and on leave) - keeps
            # LeaderboardManager's leave-time snapshot correct whatever the handler order.
            Persisted := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player).Level
            if (Persisted >= 1) then Persisted else 1

    GetPoints<public>(Player : player)<transacts> : int=
        if (Points := PlayerPoints[Player]):
            Points
        else:
            GetPersistentSnapshot(Player).Points

    # --- Setup ---
    OnBegin<override>()<suspends> : void=
        var TotalTriggers : int = 0
        var EventIndex : int = 0
        for (Event : ScoreEvents):
            set EventIndex += 1
            Count := SubscribeScoreEvent(Event)
            set TotalTriggers += Count
            Log("prestige_manager: event {EventIndex} ({Event.Points} pts) -> {Count} trigger(s)")
        Log("prestige_manager: ready -> {ScoreEvents.Length} event(s), {TotalTriggers} trigger(s) total")

        GetPlayspace().PlayerAddedEvent().Subscribe(OnPlayerAdded)
        GetPlayspace().PlayerRemovedEvent().Subscribe(OnPlayerRemoved)

        # --- T-064: shared trigger-based VIP signaling (persistence for the prestige-100
        # bypass / hidden debug button) ---
        VipGrantTrigger.TriggeredEvent.Subscribe(OnVipGrantTriggered)

        # --- T-088 (v25): debug level triggers, only wired when explicitly enabled ---
        if (DebugTriggersEnabled?):
            DebugLevelUpTrigger.TriggeredEvent.Subscribe(OnDebugLevelUp)
            DebugLevelDownTrigger.TriggeredEvent.Subscribe(OnDebugLevelDown)
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] DEBUG level triggers ENABLED (test-only) - UP/DOWN subscribed")
        else:
            Log("prestige_manager: [T-088] DEBUG level triggers disabled")

        for (Player : GetPlayspace().GetPlayers()):
            OnPlayerAdded(Player)

    # Wires every trigger in a score_event's Triggers array to award that event's Points.
    # Returns how many triggers were actually subscribed (skipped if Points <= 0).
    SubscribeScoreEvent(Event : score_event) : int=
        var Count : int = 0
        if (Event.Points > 0):
            for (Trigger : Event.Triggers):
                Listener : score_event_listener = score_event_listener{Manager := Self, Points := Event.Points}
                Trigger.TriggeredEvent.Subscribe(Listener.OnTriggered)
                set Count += 1
        else:
            Log("prestige_manager: an event has trigger(s) configured but Points <= 0 — skipped")
        Count

    # --- Player tracking ---
    # v5: restores persisted points/level from the native Verse weak_map instead of the two
    # removed Tracker Devices. Epic's persistence system auto-loads each player's previously
    # saved `prestige_persistent_data` entry into `PrestigeData` when they join - by the time
    # this handler runs, `PrestigeData[Player]` already holds the restored value if one exists.
    # A brand-new player has no entry at all (`PrestigeData[Player]` fails), in which case we
    # seed a fresh default (Points=0, Level=1) and write it once so later reads/writes have
    # something to update.
    OnPlayerAdded(Player : player) : void=
        var RestoredPoints : int = 0
        var RestoredLevel : int = 1
        var RestoredHasVip : logic = false
        if (Existing := PrestigeData[Player]):
            set RestoredPoints = Existing.Points
            set RestoredLevel = Existing.Level
            set RestoredHasVip = Existing.HasVipPermanent
        else:
            if (set PrestigeData[Player] = prestige_persistent_data{}) {}
        if (set PlayerPoints[Player] = RestoredPoints, set PlayerLevel[Player] = RestoredLevel):
            Log("prestige_manager: player joined, restored prestige - level {RestoredLevel}, {RestoredPoints} pts into it")

        # --- T-063 v14 (circular-dependency fix): PUSH the persisted VIP flag onto Vip_Manager
        # directly (via the existing one-way VipManagerRef from T-054), instead of Vip_Manager
        # pulling it via a reverse device-ref. Single source of truth stays here; Vip_Manager
        # only ever receives the outcome.
        if (RestoredHasVip?):
            VipManagerRef.ApplyVipOwnership(Player, true)
            Log("prestige_manager: pushed persisted VIP status onto Vip_Manager for a rejoining player")

        # v25 (T-088): join/rejoin - compute the target aura directly from the persisted level and
        # assign it (cleanup first, then only that aura's trigger). Per-player, no shared state.
        ApplyAuraForLevel(Player, 0, RestoredLevel, "join")
        # The per-player WB_Main widget is built by coin_display_manager (driven by GameManager,
        # a fully independent device from this one) - it may not exist yet the instant this
        # event fires. A short deferred push picks it up once it's ready without this module
        # ever calling into GameManager/coin_display_manager beyond the read-only getter.
        spawn{ PushInitialWidgetState(Player) }

    # v5: belt-and-braces persist on disconnect, same reasoning as before (in case a disconnect
    # races a just-applied award) - just writing the weak_map entry now instead of calling
    # Tracker Device Save().
    OnPlayerRemoved(Player : player) : void=
        PersistPrestige(Player)
        Log("prestige_manager: player left, prestige state saved to persistent storage")
        # v21 (T-073): prune the session cache AFTER persisting (never before - data loss).
        if (NewPoints := PlayerPoints.WithRemovedKey(Player)?):
            set PlayerPoints = NewPoints
        if (NewLevels := PlayerLevel.WithRemovedKey(Player)?):
            set PlayerLevel = NewLevels

    # v5: single write-point for the persistent weak_map entry, used by both AwardPoints and
    # OnPlayerRemoved. `FitsInPlayerMap` is Epic's own guard against exceeding the 256KB/player
    # persistent-storage limit before committing a write - two ints never comes close, but this
    # is the documented safe pattern to follow rather than writing unconditionally.
    PersistPrestige(Player : player) : void=
        FinalPoints := if (P := PlayerPoints[Player]) then P else 0
        FinalLevel := if (L := PlayerLevel[Player]) then L else 1
        # v8 (T-037): carry the lifetime-stat fields forward from the current snapshot - this
        # class now has more than Points/Level, and a class literal not mentioning a field resets
        # it to its default, so Kills/GoldEarned/DiamondsEarned must be re-read and re-specified
        # every time this writes, or they'd silently zero out on every prestige award.
        CurrentSnapshot := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player)
        UpdatedData := CopyPrestigeData(CurrentSnapshot, ?Points := option{FinalPoints}, ?Level := option{FinalLevel})
        if (FitsInPlayerMap[UpdatedData]):
            if (set PrestigeData[Player] = UpdatedData) {}

    # --- v8 (T-037): lifetime leaderboard stats - public read/write API for LeaderboardManager.
    # Never decremented, independent of PlayerPoints/PlayerLevel above.
    GetKills<public>(Player : player)<transacts> : int=
        GetPersistentSnapshot(Player).Kills

    GetGoldEarned<public>(Player : player)<transacts> : int=
        GetPersistentSnapshot(Player).GoldEarned

    GetDiamondsEarned<public>(Player : player)<transacts> : int=
        GetPersistentSnapshot(Player).DiamondsEarned

    AddKill<public>(Player : player) : void=
        Snapshot := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player)
        Updated := CopyPrestigeData(Snapshot, ?Kills := option{Snapshot.Kills + 1})
        WritePersistentSnapshot(Player, Updated)

    AddGoldEarned<public>(Player : player, Amount : int) : void=
        Snapshot := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player)
        Updated := CopyPrestigeData(Snapshot, ?GoldEarned := option{Snapshot.GoldEarned + Amount})
        WritePersistentSnapshot(Player, Updated)

    AddDiamondsEarned<public>(Player : player, Amount : int) : void=
        Snapshot := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player)
        Updated := CopyPrestigeData(Snapshot, ?DiamondsEarned := option{Snapshot.DiamondsEarned + Amount})
        WritePersistentSnapshot(Player, Updated)

    # v20 (T-070): batched write - adds all three lifetime deltas in ONE persistent write.
    AddLifetimeStats<public>(Player : player, Kills : int, Gold : int, Diamonds : int) : void=
        if (Kills > 0 or Gold > 0 or Diamonds > 0):
            Snapshot := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player)
            Updated := CopyPrestigeData(Snapshot, ?Kills := option{Snapshot.Kills + Kills}, ?GoldEarned := option{Snapshot.GoldEarned + Gold}, ?DiamondsEarned := option{Snapshot.DiamondsEarned + Diamonds})
            WritePersistentSnapshot(Player, Updated)

    # --- v9 (T-040): unlocked-area persistence for AreaUnlockManager.verse, reusing this class's
    # weak_map (see field header note above for why). Read-through / write-through only - this
    # module makes no assumption about what the indices mean, it's purely a storage delegate.
    GetUnlockedAreaIndices<public>(Player : player)<transacts> : []int=
        GetPersistentSnapshot(Player).UnlockedAreaIndices

    SetUnlockedAreaIndices<public>(Player : player, UnlockedAreaIndices : []int) : void=
        Snapshot := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player)
        Updated := CopyPrestigeData(Snapshot, ?UnlockedAreaIndices := option{UnlockedAreaIndices})
        WritePersistentSnapshot(Player, Updated)

    # --- v10 (T-037): MAX ROUND REACHED - a MAXIMUM, not a cumulative total (unlike Kills/
    # GoldEarned/DiamondsEarned above). "Reached while connected" semantics: the caller
    # (LeaderboardManager.verse) calls UpdateMaxRoundReached for every CURRENTLY CONNECTED
    # player whenever a new round starts - a player who disconnected before that round simply
    # never receives the call for it, which is the correct "reached while connected" behavior
    # with no extra bookkeeping needed here. Write-only-if-higher, so a stale/late call can never
    # lower an already-recorded max.
    GetMaxRoundReached<public>(Player : player)<transacts> : int=
        GetPersistentSnapshot(Player).MaxRoundReached

    UpdateMaxRoundReached<public>(Player : player, CurrentRound : int) : void=
        Snapshot := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player)
        if (CurrentRound > Snapshot.MaxRoundReached):
            Updated := CopyPrestigeData(Snapshot, ?MaxRoundReached := option{CurrentRound})
            WritePersistentSnapshot(Player, Updated)
            Log("prestige_manager: new max round reached for a player - {CurrentRound}")

    # --- v13 (T-063): persisted VIP flag accessors (single source of truth). GetHasVip/SetHasVip read/write
    # prestige_persistent_data.HasVipPermanent; SetHasVip is called from this module (ApplyLevelUps on the
    # prestige-100 crossing, and OnVipGrantTriggered). Vip_Manager never calls into this module; on rejoin
    # OnPlayerAdded reads the flag directly and pushes it via VipManagerRef.ApplyVipOwnership.
    # (The Marketplace/entitlement handling and GetVipPrestigeLevelThreshold that earlier notes mention were removed.)
    #
    #
    #
    GetHasVip<public>(Player : player)<transacts> : logic=
        GetPersistentSnapshot(Player).HasVipPermanent

    SetHasVip<public>(Player : player, Value : logic) : void=
        Snapshot := GetPersistentSnapshot(Player)
        Updated := CopyPrestigeData(Snapshot, ?HasVipPermanent := option{Value})
        WritePersistentSnapshot(Player, Updated)
        ValueText : string = if (Value?) then "true" else "false"
        Log("prestige_manager: persisted unified VIP flag set to {ValueText} for a player")

    # T-107: the unused GetShieldLevel/SetShieldLevel (and Health/Speed/Damage) delegates were
    # removed. The UpgradeLevel* fields of prestige_persistent_data stay untouched on purpose
    # (removing a persistable field would reset players' saved data).

    # --- T-064: trigger-based VIP persistence handler ---
    # OnVipGrantTriggered (renamed from v14's OnVipGrantedExternally, T-064 - the Marketplace
    # purchase path that name referenced no longer exists; the only remaining callers are the
    # prestige-100 crossing and the hidden debug button): PrestigeManager subscribes to its OWN
    # existing VipGrantTrigger, covering persistence for the hidden debug button (the prestige-100
    # crossing path in ApplyLevelUps below sets the flag directly instead of relying on this
    # handler, since it's the same player and simplest to just set it there).
    # v16 (B-030 fix): the level check is deliberately SKIPPED for whether the grant itself is
    # allowed to happen (the hidden VipBonusTestButton must keep working below level
    # VipPrestigeLevelThreshold for dev/te

# ViridumConversationUI.verse
# Summary: Thin per-player wrapper around the stock Personadevice.UW_Conversation03 widget
#   (transcript-style Astra conversation UI, T-011/T-045). The widget class exposes only plain
#   data fields (PersonaName, PersonaMessage, StatusMessage, IsRecording, IsProcessing,
#   IsPlayingAudio, ShowActionWidget, CloseEvent, ...), so this wrapper implements the state
#   behavior by writing those fields. welcome_persona_device owns one instance per player in the
#   activation volume. Class/file name kept as "Viridum" (Astra persona; no mass rename).
#   Decisions: InputMode.None so movement and native push-to-talk keep working (the on-screen
#   Leave button may then not be clickable - open owner re-test); CloseEvent is awaited in a
#   background task that is cancelled via CancelWatch when the UI is removed (T-107).
# Last modified: 2026-11-05 -- v5
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/UI }
using { Personadevice }

# --- Localized UI copy (project convention, see DailyRewards/daily_rewards_device.verse) ---
ViridumListeningStatus<localizes>():message = "Listening..."
ViridumThinkingStatus<localizes>():message = "Thinking..."
ViridumIdleStatus<localizes>():message = ""
ViridumUnavailableStatus<localizes>():message = "Astra is unavailable right now, try again in a moment."

viridum_conversation_ui := class:
    var Widget : ?UW_Conversation03 = false

    # Stored so the CloseEvent handler (fired when the player clicks the widget's own
    # Leave button) can remove the widget without needing an external caller to hand the
    # player_ui back in - see BuildUI/OnCloseClicked below.
    var StoredPlayerUI : ?player_ui = false

    # Per-UI cancel signal: ends the WatchForClose task when the UI is removed or rebuilt, so
    # no task is left waiting on a widget that is gone (T-107 finding 9-15 / item a).
    CancelWatch : event() = event(){}

    # --- Lifecycle: add/remove the widget from this player's player_ui ---
    BuildUI(PlayerUI : player_ui, PersonaDisplayName : message) : void=
        # End any watcher left from a previous build of this UI.
        CancelWatch.Signal()
        NewWidget := UW_Conversation03:
            PersonaName := PersonaDisplayName
            PersonaMessage := ViridumIdleStatus()
            StatusMessage := ViridumIdleStatus()
            IsRecording := false
            IsProcessing := false
            IsPlayingAudio := false
            ShowActionWidget := true
            TimeLeftForAudioRecordingNormalized := 0.0

        # `None`, not `All` - see file header (2026-09-10 fix): this HUD must not consume
        # movement or the native push-to-talk key.
        Slot := player_ui_slot:
            InputMode := ui_input_mode.None
            ZOrder := 100

        PlayerUI.AddWidget(NewWidget, Slot)
        set Widget = option{NewWidget}
        set StoredPlayerUI = option{PlayerUI}
        # `CloseEvent`'s declared type is `event(tuple())` (confirmed via BuildAll compiler
        # error - it has no `Subscribe` member, unlike the `listenable(...)`-typed persona
        # events elsewhere in this task). Verse's `event` type is instead awaited with
        # `Await()<suspends>`, so this needs its own background task.
        spawn{WatchForClose(NewWidget)}

    # Races the widget's Leave button against the per-UI cancel event; only a real click
    # triggers OnCloseClicked, a cancel just ends the task.
    WatchForClose(W : UW_Conversation03)<suspends>:void=
        var Clicked : logic = false
        race:
            block:
                W.CloseEvent.Await()
                set Clicked = true
            CancelWatch.Await()
        if (Clicked?):
            OnCloseClicked()

    RemoveUI(PlayerUI : player_ui) : void=
        CancelWatch.Signal()
        if (W := Widget?):
            PlayerUI.RemoveWidget(W)
        set Widget = false
        set StoredPlayerUI = false

    # --- Widget's own Leave button (see file header - residual doubt on click delivery
    #     under InputMode.None) ---
    OnCloseClicked() : void=
        if (PlayerUI := StoredPlayerUI?):
            RemoveUI(PlayerUI)

    # --- State updates driven by persona_component events ---
    SetRecordingState(Recording : logic) : void=
        if (W := Widget?):
            set W.IsRecording = Recording
            if (Recording?):
                set W.StatusMessage = ViridumListeningStatus()

    UpdateRecordingProgress(Normalized : float) : void=
        if (W := Widget?):
            set W.TimeLeftForAudioRecordingNormalized = Normalized

    SetProcessingState(Processing : logic) : void=
        if (W := Widget?):
            set W.IsProcessing = Processing
            if (Processing?):
                set W.StatusMessage = ViridumThinkingStatus()

    SetSpeakingState(Speaking : logic) : void=
        if (W := Widget?):
            set W.IsPlayingAudio = Speaking

    ShowPersonaAnswer(Answer : message) : void=
        if (W := Widget?):
            set W.PersonaMessage = Answer
            set W.StatusMessage = ViridumIdleStatus()

    # Never leaves the widget stuck mid-recording/processing/speaking (kit rule 3/step 5).
    SetUnavailableState() : void=
        if (W := Widget?):
            set W.IsRecording = false
            set W.IsProcessing = false
            set W.IsPlayingAudio = false
            set W.StatusMessage = ViridumUnavailableStatus()

    SetCanSpeakState() : void=
        if (W := Widget?):
            set W.IsRecording = false
            set W.IsProcessing = false
            set W.IsPlayingAudio = false
            set W.StatusMessage = ViridumIdleStatus()

# viridum_npc_behavior.verse
# Summary: T-011, content reworked under T-045 - custom NPC Behavior for the welcome persona
#   NPC, now "Astra" (formerly "Viridum" - class/file names kept as-is, see T-045 note below),
#   assigned in WelcomeBot's NPCCharacterDefinition ("NPC Character Definition" -> "NPC
#   Character Behavior" section -> "Verse Behavior" slot in the Details panel - manual owner
#   action, see report). Owns ALL conversation-target/voice-channel setup for Astra:
#   `welcome_persona_device` (same folder)
#   no longer calls SetConversationTarget/ClearConversationTarget or creates a voice_channel/
#   agent_group directly - that responsibility was moved here per the 2026-09-10 design
#   correction in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-viridum-welcome-persona-design.md.
#
#   Base class confirmed against Epic's own sources (both consulted before writing this file,
#   not guessed):
#     - Verse API reference for `npc_behavior`
#       (https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/fortnite/verse-api/fortnitedotcom/ai/npc_behavior)
#       - module `/Fortnite.com/AI`, "Inherit from this to create a custom NPC behavior", no
#       data members, members are OnBegin<override>()<suspends>:void, OnEnd<override>():void,
#       GetAgent[]:agent (decides), GetEntity[]:entity (decides).
#     - "Add an NPC to a Conversation in Unreal Editor for Fortnite" doc - its own
#       `persona_npc_behavior` sample is declared `class(npc_behavior)`, and explicitly notes
#       its stock `OnBegin` (`AddPlayersAsConversationTarget()`, adding EVERY current player
#       immediately) is the wrong default for a "player walks up via a trigger" case like ours.
#   This class mirrors that shape under a different name (so it coexists with any stock sample
#   left in the project) and deliberately does NOT call an add-everyone method from OnBegin -
#   conversation targets are added/removed strictly per player, driven externally by
#   `welcome_persona_device` from `Volume.AgentEntersEvent`/`AgentExitsEvent`.
#
#   Cross-file wiring note: Epic's docs/API reference expose no getter for an external
#   creative_device to retrieve the npc_behavior instance running on a spawned NPC entity
#   (confirmed: `npc_behavior` has no data members and no reverse entity->behavior lookup is
#   documented anywhere in the two sources above). A module-level shared var was tried first and
#   rejected by the compiler: "Module-scoped `var` must have `weak_map` type" restricted to a
#   `session`/`player` key (confirmed via BuildAll) - `entity` isn't a valid key, and a bare
#   optional isn't a valid module var at all. Instead this file uses Epic's own documented
#   tag-based lookup ("Verse Tags in Fortnite" doc): this class finds the `welcome_persona_device`
#   instance via `NPCEntity.FindCreativeObjectsWithTag(viridum_welcome_device_tag)` and casts the
#   result with the `welcome_persona_device[...]` failable cast, then calls
#   `Device.RegisterBehavior(Self)` so the device can hold an ordinary (non-module-scoped)
#   instance var pointing back at this behavior. Manual owner action required: tag the
#   `welcome_persona_device` instance in the Details panel's Tags section with
#   `viridum_welcome_device_tag` (see task report).
#
#   to "Astra" (eccentric cosmic heroine) - comments below updated to refer to the character
#   as Astra. Class/file/tag names (`viridum_npc_behavior`, `viridum_welcome_device_tag`,
#   `viridum_behavior_voice_member_info`) were left unchanged: a full identifier rename was
#   judged not trivially safe here (cross-file tag lookup wiring, manual owner-configured
#   Details-panel tag binding - see T-045 task report) and is left as a follow-up task if
#   wanted. No functional change in this file.
#
#   player_state_utils.WithRemovedKey in RemovePlayerAsConversationTarget (after the chat
#   channel is removed), so they no longer grow with every player who ever talked to Astra.
# Last modified: 2026-10-02 -- v3
using { /Fortnite.com/AI }
using { /Fortnite.com/Devices }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Conversations }
using { /Verse.org/AgentGroup }
using { /Verse.org/Chat }
using { /Verse.org/SceneGraph }
using { /Verse.org/Simulation }
using { /Verse.org/Simulation/Tags }
using { player_state_utils }

# --- Tag used to locate the `welcome_persona_device` instance from this behavior (see header
#     note). Must be assigned to that device instance's Tags in the UEFN Details panel - manual
#     owner action, see task report. ---
viridum_welcome_device_tag<public> := class(tag){}

# Voice member info for the per-player conversation pairing. Kept local to this file (distinct
# from welcome_persona_device's own, now-removed `viridum_voice_member_info`) since this class
# now owns the pairing. `has_voice_member_info` requires a mutable `CanBroadcast` field, which
# Verse structs cannot hold ("Structs may not contain mutable members") and cannot inherit an
# interface either ("Structs may not inherit from any other types") - a class is required.
viridum_behavior_voice_member_info<public> := class(has_voice_member_info):
    var CanBroadcast<override>:logic = true

# --- Custom NPC Behavior: per-player conversation-target/voice-channel setup for Viridum ---
viridum_npc_behavior<public> := class(npc_behavior):

    # Centralized logger (see Claude/reference/logger-template.verse.txt).
    @editable DebugLoggingEnabled : logic = true
    Log(LogMessage : string) : void=
        if (DebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Print(LogMessage)

    ChannelName<localizes>:message = "AstraConversation"

    # Found once in OnBegin - the WelcomeBot NPCCharacterDefinition asset already carries a
    # `persona_component` (Prompt Editor Tool content); this class finds it, doesn't add one.
    # Same discovery pattern as welcome_persona_device.OnPersonaSpawned (no GetOrAddComponent/
    # GetComponent[] API confirmed on entity in this project's digests - FindDescendantComponents
    # is used instead).
    var PersonaComponent : ?persona_component = false

    # The `welcome_persona_device` instance found via tag lookup in OnBegin (see header) -
    # cached so OnEnd can clear the device's back-reference on despawn.
    var LinkedDevice : ?welcome_persona_device = false

    # Per-player agent_group/voice_channel pairs. Multiplayer (kit rule 3): each player added
    # via AddPlayerAsConversationTarget gets an independent pairing - up to 4 in parallel, one
    # player's conversation state never affects another's. Stale map entries left after a
    # removal are harmless (same reasoning as welcome_persona_device's own per-player maps):
    # every field they reference is already torn down, and the entry is fully overwritten the
    # next time that same player is added again. Verse's native map type has no key-removal API.
    var PlayerGroups : [player]agent_group(viridum_behavior_voice_member_info) = map{}
    var PlayerChannels : [player]voice_channel(viridum_behavior_voice_member_info) = map{}

    # --- Lifecycle: register this instance for external lookup, find the persona_component,
    #     and deliberately do NOT add every current player as a conversation target (see
    #     header - that's the stock persona_npc_behavior sample's default, wrong for us). ---
    OnBegin<override>()<suspends>:void=
        if (NPCEntity := GetEntity[]):
            # Find persona_component (same discovery pattern as
            # welcome_persona_device.OnPersonaSpawned).
            var FoundPersona : ?persona_component = false
            for (Candidate : NPCEntity.FindDescendantComponents(persona_component)):
                if (not FoundPersona?):
                    set FoundPersona = option{Candidate}
            set PersonaComponent = FoundPersona
            if (FoundPersona?):
                Log("viridum_npc_behavior: persona_component found on Astra, awaiting per-player AddPlayerAsConversationTarget calls (no auto-add-all)")
            else:
                Log("viridum_npc_behavior: [WARN] no persona_component found on entity - check WelcomeBot's NPCCharacterDefinition asset")

            # Find welcome_persona_device via tag lookup (see header) and register with it so
            # it can call our public API from Volume.AgentEntersEvent/AgentExitsEvent.
            var FoundDevice : ?welcome_persona_device = false
            for (Obj : NPCEntity.FindCreativeObjectsWithTag(viridum_welcome_device_tag)):
                if (not FoundDevice?, Device := welcome_persona_device[Obj]):
                    set FoundDevice = option{Device}
            if (Device := FoundDevice?):
                set LinkedDevice = FoundDevice
                Device.RegisterBehavior(Self)
                Log("viridum_npc_behavior: registered with welcome_persona_device")
            else:
                Log("viridum_npc_behavior: [WARN] no welcome_persona_device found with viridum_welcome_device_tag - tag the device instance in its Details panel")
        else:
            Log("viridum_npc_behavior: [WARN] OnBegin - GetEntity[] failed, cannot find persona_component/device")

    OnEnd<override>():void=
        for (Player -> Group : PlayerGroups):
            RemovePlayerAsConversationTarget(Player)
        if (Device := LinkedDevice?):
            Device.ClearBehavior()
        Log("viridum_npc_behavior: OnEnd - all players removed from conversation")

    # --- Public API called by welcome_persona_device from Volume.AgentEntersEvent ---
    # `<transacts>` required for AddChatChannel/SetConversationTarget/map-index writes, which
    # carry the native `no_rollback` effect (see uefn-lessons).
    AddPlayerAsConversationTarget(Player:player):void=
        if:
            Persona := PersonaComponent?
            NPCAgent := GetAgent[]
            NPCEntity := GetEntity[]
        then:
            Group : agent_group(viridum_behavior_voice_member_info) = agent_group(viridum_behavior_voice_member_info){}
            # `AddMember`/`AddChatChannel` return `result(...)`, not a `<decides>` value - called
            # as plain statements, not branched on (same approach welcome_persona_device used
            # before this refactor).
            Group.AddMember(Player, viridum_behavior_voice_member_info{})
            Group.AddMember(NPCAgent, viridum_behavior_voice_member_info{})

            Channel : voice_channel(viridum_behavior_voice_member_info) = voice_channel(viridum_behavior_voice_member_info):
                Name := ChannelName
                Group := Group

            NPCEntity.AddChatChannel(Channel)
            if (set PlayerGroups[Player] = Group):
                if (set PlayerChannels[Player] = Channel):
                    Player.SetConversationTarget(Persona, Channel)
                    Log("viridum_npc_behavior: player added as conversation target")
        else:
            Log("viridum_npc_behavior: [WARN] AddPlayerAsConversationTarget - missing persona/agent/entity, skipping")

    # --- Public API called by welcome_persona_device from Volume.AgentExitsEvent ---
    RemovePlayerAsConversationTarget(Player:player):void=
        Player.ClearConversationTarget()
        if (Channel := PlayerChannels[Player]):
            if (NPCEntity := GetEntity[]):
                NPCEntity.RemoveChatChannel(Channel)
        # T-086: prune only after the channel/group were torn down above.
        if (NewChannels := PlayerChannels.WithRemovedKey(Player)?):
            set PlayerChannels = NewChannels
        if (NewGroups := PlayerGroups.WithRemovedKey(Player)?):
            set PlayerGroups = NewGroups
        Log("viridum_npc_behavior: player removed from conversation")

    # --- Public API: send the auto-greeting prompt for a given player using that player's own
    #     channel (kept encapsulated here rather than exposing the channel itself to the
    #     device). Returns whether the prompt was accepted (mirrors persona_component's own
    #     PromptToTalk decides-semantics, converted to a plain logic for the caller). ---
    PromptToTalk(Player:player, Instructions:message):logic=
        if:
            Persona := PersonaComponent?
            Channel := PlayerChannels[Player]
            Persona.PromptToTalk[Instructions, Channel]
        then:
            true
        else:
            false

# welcome_persona_device.verse
# Summary: T-045 (content rework of T-011) - orchestrates the "Astra" welcome NPC (formerly
#   "Viridum") using UEFN's native Persona/LLM system (no external LLM integration). On NPC
#   spawn, finds the `persona_component` the WelcomeBot NPCCharacterDefinition asset already
#   carries and wires its events. When a player enters `Volume`, this device does NOT set up
#   the conversation target/voice-channel itself (2026-09-10 design correction) - it calls
#   into the running `viridum_npc_behavior` instance (`ActiveBehavior`, registered by that
#   class via `RegisterBehavior` - see its header for how it finds this device) - its
#   `AddPlayerAsConversationTarget`/`PromptToTalk`. On exit, it
#   calls the behavior's `RemovePlayerAsConversationTarget`. This device still owns the
#   `ViridumConversationUI` widget lifecycle and the persona event -> widget-state wiring
#   (StartHear/StopHear/StartSay/StopSay/CommitSay/PromptFailure) - only the conversation-
#   target/voice-channel plumbing moved out, into `viridum_npc_behavior.verse` (same folder).
#   `PersonaSpawner` and `Volume` are gameplay-critical in position (where the NPC stands / the
#   activation area) and are never moved onto a DemoDisplay stand - see demo_welcomePersona.
#   NOTE: the behavior class, tag, and UI class names still say `viridum`/`Viridum` (file
#   `viridum_npc_behavior.verse`, `ViridumConversationUI.verse`, tag
#   `viridum_welcome_device_tag`) - a full identifier/file rename was judged not trivially
#   safe (cross-file references, tag lookups, manual owner-configured bindings) and is left as
#   a follow-up task; only display text/content was reworked for T-045. See T-045 task report.
#
#   Reference-implementation note: the original Epic example this pattern was modeled on
#   (`custom_verse/Personadevice/esempi/ui_conversations_device.verse`) was removed from the
#   project before this file was written. Every API used below was re-verified directly
#   against this project's own generated Verse digests (UnrealEngine.digest.verse,
#   Verse.digest.verse, Fortnite.digest.verse, root_harrow-Assets.digest.verse) rather than
#   assumed from memory of the deleted example - see the per-section notes for anything that
#   turned out to differ from the design spec's expectations.
#
#   `agent_group`/`voice_channel` creation previously here were moved to `viridum_npc_behavior`
#   (assigned on WelcomeBot's NPCCharacterDefinition "Verse Behavior" slot - manual owner
#   action, see task report), per Epic's own doc ("Add an NPC to a Conversation in UEFN"):
#   that setup is not something a `creative_device` does on its own, it requires a dedicated
#   NPC Behavior class. See viridum_npc_behavior.verse's header for the full rationale and the
#   base-class/registry sourcing.
#
#   to "Astra" (eccentric cosmic heroine) - display name and auto-greeting trigger text
#   updated below; no architectural/functional change (wiring, UI lifecycle, retention hooks
#   all unchanged).
#
#   comment justifying the all-players reset, matching OnPromptFailure's existing one, since
#   StopSayEvent also carries no player identity - documented as an accepted Persona-API
#   limitation rather than a bug. (2) Added GetPlayspace().PlayerRemovedEvent() subscription /
#   OnPlayerRemoved handler to tear down a disconnecting player's conversation-target/voice-
#   channel pairing even when they disconnect without walking out of Volume first (previously
#   only OnAgentExitsVolume did this teardown).
#
#   volume exit and on player removal; persona event subscriptions stored and cancelled on NPC
#   despawn (ClearBehavior) and before re-wiring on respawn; per-player "Thinking..." timeout
#   (ThinkingTimeoutSeconds) resets the widget to the unavailable state if no StartSay/
#   PromptFailure arrives. Per-player timer tokens are invalidated/pruned on answer, exit, leave.
# Last modified: 2026-10-02 -- v5
using { /Verse.org/Simulation }
using { /Verse.org/SceneGraph }
using { /Verse.org/AgentGroup }
using { /Verse.org/Chat }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Conversations }
using { /UnrealEngine.com/Temporary/UI }
using { /Fortnite.com/Devices }
using { /Fortnite.com/Characters }
using { /<Account>@fortnite.com/<Project>/custom_verse/player_state_utils }

welcome_persona_device := class(creative_device):

    # Centralized logger (see Claude/reference/logger-template.verse.txt). Class member, not
    # file-level, so it shows up as a configurable property in the Details panel (known
    # project pattern, see GameManager.verse).
    @editable DebugLoggingEnabled : logic = true
    Log(LogMessage : string) : void=
        if (DebugLoggingEnabled?):
            Print(LogMessage)

    # --- Editable device references (gameplay-critical position - never moved, see header) ---
    @editable PersonaSpawner : npc_spawner_device = npc_spawner_device{}
    @editable Volume : volume_device = volume_device{}

    # --- Persona runtime state (single NPC, set once on spawn) ---
    var PersonaComponent : ?persona_component = false
    var PersonaAgent : ?agent = false
    var PersonaEntity : ?entity = false

    # The running viridum_npc_behavior instance, registered via RegisterBehavior (called by
    # that class's OnBegin after it finds this device through a tag lookup - see
    # viridum_npc_behavior.verse's header for why: no Epic-documented API exists for a
    # creative_device to retrieve the npc_behavior instance running on a spawned NPC entity).
    # Manual owner action required: tag this device instance with `viridum_welcome_device_tag`
    # in its Details panel (see task report).
    var ActiveBehavior : ?viridum_npc_behavior = false

    # --- Per-player conversation state. Multiplayer (kit rule 3): each player who enters the
    #     volume gets their own UI instance - up to 4 in parallel, independent of one another.
    #     Per-player group/channel state now lives in viridum_npc_behavior instead (2026-09-10
    #     correction) - this device only tracks the UI widget per player. Stale map entries left
    #     after an exit are harmless: every field they reference is already torn down in
    #     OnAgentExitsVolume, and the entry is fully overwritten the next time that same player
    #     enters again. Verse's native map type has no key-removal API to rely on instead. ---
    #     v5 (T-086): entries are now pruned on exit/leave (WithRemovedKey). ---
    var PlayerUIs : [player]viridum_conversation_ui = map{}

    # --- v5 (T-086): max seconds the widget may stay in "Thinking..." with no StartSay/
    #     PromptFailure before it is reset to the unavailable state ---
    @editable ThinkingTimeoutSeconds : float = 20.0

    # Per-player armed timeout token (task.Cancel is not callable here, so a timer is "cancelled" by
    # pruning/replacing its token; a stale timer sees a mismatched token on wake-up and does nothing).
    var ThinkingTimers : [player]int = map{}
    var NextThinkingToken : int = 0

    # Persona event subscriptions, kept so they can be cancelled on NPC despawn / respawn.
    var PersonaSubscriptions : []cancelable = array{}

    OnBegin<override>()<suspends>:void=
        PersonaSpawner.SpawnedEvent.Subscribe(OnPersonaSpawned)
        Volume.AgentEntersEvent.Subscribe(OnAgentEntersVolume)
        Volume.AgentExitsEvent.Subscribe(OnAgentExitsVolume)
        # Disconnect-mid-conversation (verse-reviewer follow-up, 2026-09-14): a player who
        # disconnects while still inside Volume never fires AgentExitsEvent, so without this
        # subscription their conversation-target/voice-channel pairing in viridum_npc_behavior
        # and their PlayerUIs entry here would never be torn down - unlike the harmless stale
        # map-entry case documented on PlayerUIs above (overwritten on re-entry), a disconnected
        # player never comes back to overwrite it. GetPlayspace().PlayerRemovedEvent() is this
        # project's established pattern for this (see GameManager.verse, Playtime_manager.verse).
        GetPlayspace().PlayerRemovedEvent().Subscribe(OnPlayerRemoved)
        Log("welcome_persona_device: subscribed to spawner/volume/playspace events")

    # --- Spawn: the WelcomeBot NPCCharacterDefinition asset already carries a
    #     `persona_component` (Prompt Editor Tool content) - find it, don't add one. No
    #     `GetOrAddComponent` API exists on `entity` in this project's Verse digests; component
    #     discovery goes through `FindDescendantComponents`. ---
    OnPersonaSpawned(SpawnedAgent : agent) : void=
        set PersonaAgent = option{SpawnedAgent}
        if:
            FortChar := SpawnedAgent.GetFortCharacter[]
            NPCEntity := FortChar.GetEntity[]
        then:
            set PersonaEntity = option{NPCEntity}
            var FoundPersona : ?persona_component = false
            for (Candidate : NPCEntity.FindDescendantComponents(persona_component)):
                if (not FoundPersona?):
                    set FoundPersona = option{Candidate}
            if (Persona := FoundPersona?):
                set PersonaComponent = option{Persona}
                # Drop any subscriptions from a previous spawn before re-wiring (T-086).
                CancelPersonaSubscriptions()
                set PersonaSubscriptions += array{
                    Persona.StartHearEvent.Subscribe(OnStartHear),
                    Persona.StopHearEvent.Subscribe(OnStopHear),
                    Persona.StartSayEvent.Subscribe(OnStartSay),
                    Persona.StopSayEvent.Subscribe(OnStopSay),
                    Persona.CommitSayEvent.Subscribe(OnCommitSay),
                    Persona.PromptFailureEvent.Subscribe(OnPromptFailure)}
                Log("welcome_persona_device: persona_component found on Viridum, events wired")
            else:
                Log("welcome_persona_device: [WARN] spawned NPC entity has no persona_component - check WelcomeBot's NPCCharacterDefinition asset")
        else:
            Log("welcome_persona_device: [WARN] could not resolve fort_character/entity for spawned NPC agent")

    # --- Called by viridum_npc_behavior.OnBegin once it finds this device via tag lookup ---
    RegisterBehavior(Behavior:viridum_npc_behavior):void=
        set ActiveBehavior = option{Behavior}
        Log("welcome_persona_device: viridum_npc_behavior registered")

    # --- Called by viridum_npc_behavior.OnEnd on NPC despawn ---
    ClearBehavior():void=
        set ActiveBehavior = false
        CancelPersonaSubscriptions()
        for (Player -> Token : ThinkingTimers):
            CancelThinkingTimer(Player)
        Log("welcome_persona_device: viridum_npc_behavior cleared (NPC despawned)")

    # --- T-086: cancel every stored persona event subscription (NPC despawn / respawn) ---
    CancelPersonaSubscriptions() : void=
        for (Subscription : PersonaSubscriptions):
            Subscription.Cancel()
        set PersonaSubscriptions = array{}

    # --- T-086: cancel and prune a player's "Thinking..." timeout task, if any ---
    CancelThinkingTimer(Player : player) : void=
        if (NewTimers := ThinkingTimers.WithRemovedKey(Player)?):
            set ThinkingTimers = NewTimers

    # --- T-086: remove a player's widget reference (after the widget itself was torn down) ---
    PrunePlayerUI(Player : player) : void=
        if (NewUIs := PlayerUIs.WithRemovedKey(Player)?):
            set PlayerUIs = NewUIs

    # --- T-086: if no StartSay/PromptFailure arrives within ThinkingTimeoutSeconds of the player
    #     finishing speaking, reset the widget so it never stays stuck on "Thinking..." ---
    ThinkingTimeout(Player : player, UI : viridum_conversation_ui, Token : int)<suspends> : void=
        Sleep(ThinkingTimeoutSeconds)
        if (not (ThinkingTimers[Player] = Token)):
            return
        Log("welcome_persona_device: [WARN] thinking timeout - no StartSay/PromptFailure, resetting widget")
        UI.SetUnavailableState()
        if (NewTimers := ThinkingTimers.WithRemovedKey(Player)?):
            set ThinkingTimers = NewTimers

    # --- Player enters the activation volume: delegate the conversation-target/voice-channel
    #     pairing to viridum_npc_behavior (2026-09-10 correction - this device no longer calls
    #     SetConversationTarget/creates voice_channel/agent_group itself), then build the UI and
    #     send the auto-greeting via the behavior's own PromptToTalk wrapper. ---
    OnAgentEntersVolume(EnteringAgent : agent) : void=
        if:
            Player := player[EnteringAgent]
            Behavior := ActiveBehavior?
            PlayerUI := GetPlayerUI[Player]
        then:
            Behavior.AddPlayerAsConversationTarget(Player)

            UI := viridum_conversation_ui{}
            UI.BuildUI(PlayerUI, AstraPersonaDisplayName())
            if (set PlayerUIs[Player] = UI):
                # Auto-greeting: Astra speaks first, unprompted by the player. If
                # `PromptToTalk` fails (e.g. interrupt rule blocks it), surface the
                # unavailable state instead of leaving the widget looking idle/broken.
                GreetingInstructions := AstraGreetingInstructions()
                PromptAccepted : logic = Behavior.PromptToTalk(Player, GreetingInstructions)
                if (PromptAccepted?):
                    Log("welcome_persona_device: auto-greeting prompt sent to Astra")
                else:
                    UI.SetUnavailableState()
                    Log("welcome_persona_device: [WARN] PromptToTalk failed for auto-greeting (interrupt rule or persona not in channel)")
        else:
            Log("welcome_persona_device: [WARN] OnAgentEntersVolume - missing player/NPC entity/behavior instance/PlayerUI, skipping")

    # --- Player exits the activation volume: tear down everything for that player only ---
    OnAgentExitsVolume(ExitingAgent : agent) : void=
        if (Player := player[ExitingAgent]):
            if (Behavior := ActiveBehavior?):
                Behavior.RemovePlayerAsConversationTarget(Player)
            else:
                Log("welcome_persona_device: [WARN] OnAgentExitsVolume - no behavior instance registered, conversation target may linger")

            if (UI := PlayerUIs[Player]):
                if (PlayerUI := GetPlayerUI[Player]):
                    UI.RemoveUI(PlayerUI)
            CancelThinkingTimer(Player)
            PrunePlayerUI(Player)

            Log("welcome_persona_device: player exited volume, conversation torn down")
        else:
            Log("welcome_persona_device: [WARN] OnAgentExitsVolume - exiting agent is not a player")

    # --- Player disconnects entirely (may still be inside Volume - AgentExitsEvent never fires
    #     in that case). Mirrors OnAgentExitsVolume's teardown so the conversation-target/voice-
    #     channel pairing in viridum_npc_behavior doesn't linger against a player who is no
    #     longer in the session. Widget removal is best-effort: GetPlayerUI may no longer resolve
    #     for a player who has just left, in which case there's no live widget instance left to
    #     remove from anyway. ---
    OnPlayerRemoved(RemovedPlayer : player) : void=
        if (Behavior := ActiveBehavior?):
            Behavior.RemovePlayerAsConversationTarget(RemovedPlayer)
        if (UI := PlayerUIs[RemovedPlayer]):
            if (PlayerUI := GetPlayerUI[RemovedPlayer]):
                UI.RemoveUI(PlayerUI)
        CancelThinkingTimer(RemovedPlayer)
        PrunePlayerUI(RemovedPlayer)
        Log("welcome_persona_device: player disconnected, conversation torn down")

    # --- Persona event -> widget state wiring (kit rule 3/step 5: never leave the UI stuck) ---
    OnStartHear(HearingAgent : agent) : void=
        if (Player := player[HearingAgent]):
            if (UI := PlayerUIs[Player]):
                UI.SetRecordingState(true)

    OnStopHear(HearingAgent : agent) : void=
        if (Player := player[HearingAgent]):
            if (UI := PlayerUIs[Player]):
                UI.SetProcessingState(true)
                CancelThinkingTimer(Player)
                set NextThinkingToken += 1
                Token := NextThinkingToken
                if (set ThinkingTimers[Player] = Token):
                    spawn{ThinkingTimeout(Player, UI, Token)}
                    Log("welcome_persona_device: thinking timeout armed")

    OnStartSay(SayInfo : tuple(?agent, cancelable)) : void=
        if (RespondingTo := SayInfo(0)?):
            if (Player := player[RespondingTo]):
                CancelThinkingTimer(Player)
                if (UI := PlayerUIs[Player]):
                    UI.SetProcessingState(false)
                    UI.SetSpeakingState(true)

    OnCommitSay(SayResult : tuple(?agent, message)) : void=
        if (RespondingTo := SayResult(0)?):
            if (Player := player[RespondingTo]):
                if (UI := PlayerUIs[Player]):
                    UI.ShowPersonaAnswer(SayResult(1))

    # `StopSayEvent` carries only a `logic` (WasInterrupted) - no agent/player identity, same
    # documented limitation as `PromptFailureEvent` below. With multiple players concurrently
    # paired with Astra (up to 4 in parallel, see PlayerUIs header), this means every player's
    # widget is reset to "can speak" whenever ANY single player's turn ends - there is no
    # Persona-API way to scope this to only the player who was actually speaking. Accepted as a
    # known limitation of the current UEFN Persona API (re-verified against this project's
    # UnrealEngine.digest.verse - no per-agent overload exists for this event) rather than a bug
    # to silently work around; flagged for the owner if this call is confirmed reproducible in a
    # live multiplayer playtest (widget prematurely re-enabled while still mid-recording/
    # processing/speaking for another player).
    OnStopSay(WasInterrupted : logic) : void=
        for (Player -> UI : PlayerUIs):
            CancelThinkingTimer(Player)
            UI.SetSpeakingState(false)
            UI.SetCanSpeakState()

    # `ai_throttled_error` (LLM rate-limiting) and every other `ai_error` subtype are handled
    # the same way: show the unavailable state, never leave the caller stuck mid-recording/
    # processing. `PromptFailureEvent` doesn't identify which player triggered it, so every
    # player currently paired with Viridum is reset to a safe state.
    OnPromptFailure(Error : ai_error) : void=
        Log("welcome_persona_device: [WARN] PromptFailureEvent received (ai_error) - resetting all active conversation widgets to unavailable")
        for (Player -> UI : PlayerUIs):
            CancelThinkingTimer(Player)
            UI.SetUnavailableState()

AstraPersonaDisplayName<localizes>():message = "Astra"

# Content lives in the Prompt Editor Tool on WelcomeBot (see
# Claude/docs/T-045-Astra-persona-prompt.md, T-011's doc superseded) - this is only the
# trigger instruction that makes Astra speak first, unprompted, when a player arrives.
AstraGreetingInstructions<localizes>():message = "A player has just arrived. Greet them as Astra, in your usual over-the-top cosmic-heroine style."

recipes.verify: Place the device, launch a session and check the behavior of the Verse code
